title.raw: 卷二百二十七 列傳第一百十五 龐尚鵬 宋儀望 張岳 李材 陸樹德 蕭廩 賈三近 李頤 朱鴻謨 蕭彥 孫維城 謝杰 郭惟賢 萬象春 鍾化民 吳達可 Volume 227 Biographies 115: Pang Shangpeng, Song Yiwang, Zhang Yue, Li Cai, Lu Shude, Xiao Lin, Jia Sanjin, Li Yi, Zhu Hongmo, Xiao Yan, Sun Weicheng, Xie Jie, Guo Weixian, Wan Xiangchun, Zhong Huamin, Wu Dake

translations.literal: Pang Shangpeng, Song Yiwang, Zhang Yue, Li Cai, Lu Shude, Xiao Lin, Jia Sanjin, Li Yi, Zhu Hongmo, Xiao Yan
translations.idiomatic: Pang Shangpeng, Song Yiwang, Zhang Yue, Li Cai, Lu Shude, Xiao Lin, Jia Sanjin, Li Yi, Zhu Hongmo, and Xiao Yan
[Supplementary biographies:

sentences.zh: （弟雍查鐸）〉

translations.literal: Younger Brother Yong, Zha Tuo]
translations.idiomatic: Younger Brother Yong, Zha Tuo]

sentences.zh: 孫維城謝傑郭惟賢萬象春鐘化民吳達可

translations.literal: Sun Weicheng, Xie Jie, Guo Weixian, Wan Xiangchun, Zhong Huamin, Wu Dake
translations.idiomatic: Sun Weicheng, Xie Jie, Guo Weixian, Wan Xiangchun, Zhong Huamin, and Wu Dake

sentences.zh: 明年春，朝議興九邊屯、鹽。

translations.literal: The following spring, the court deliberated on reviving military colonies and the salt monopoly in the Nine Border Regions.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring, the court took up plans to revive military colonies and the salt administration across the Nine Border Regions.

sentences.zh: 擢尚鵬右僉都御史，與副都御史鄒應龍、唐繼祿分理。

translations.literal: Shangpeng was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and, together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Zou Yinglong and Tang Jilu, was assigned to divide the duties.
translations.idiomatic: Shangpeng was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and, along with Vice Censors-in-Chief Zou Yinglong and Tang Jilu, given a share of the work.

sentences.zh: 尚鵬轄兩淮、長蘆、山東三運司，兼理畿輔、河南、山東、江北、遼東屯務。

translations.literal: Shangpeng had jurisdiction over the three salt transport commissions of Liang-Huai, Changlu, and Shandong, and concurrently oversaw military colony affairs in the capital region, Henan, Shandong, Jiangbei, and Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Shangpeng oversaw the Liang-Huai, Changlu, and Shandong salt transport commissions and at the same time handled military colony affairs in the capital region, Henan, Shandong, Jiangbei, and Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 抵昌平，劾內侍張恩擅殺人，兩淮巡鹽孫以仁贓罪，皆獲譴。

translations.literal: On reaching Changping, he impeached the eunuch Zhang En for unauthorized killing, and the Liang-Huai salt inspector Sun Yiren for corruption; both were punished.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Changping, he impeached the eunuch Zhang En for killing without authorization and the Liang-Huai salt inspector Sun Yiren for corruption; both men were punished.

sentences.zh: 其秋，應龍等召還，命尚鵬兼領九邊屯務。

translations.literal: That autumn, Yinglong and the others were recalled, and Shangpeng was ordered to take charge of military colony affairs in the Nine Border Regions as well.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Yinglong and his colleagues were recalled, and Shangpeng was ordered to take on the Nine Border military colonies as well.

sentences.zh: 疏列鹽政二十事，鹺利大興。

translations.literal: In a memorial he set forth twenty items on salt administration, and salt revenues greatly increased.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne with twenty proposals on salt administration, and salt revenues rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 乃自江北躬歷九邊，先後列上屯政便宜，江北者四，薊鎮者九，遼東、宣、大者各十一，寧夏者四，甘肅者七。

translations.literal: He then personally toured the Nine Border Regions from Jiangbei and, in succession, submitted recommendations on colony administration: four for Jiangbei, nine for Jizhen, eleven each for Liaodong and Xuan-Da, four for Ningxia, and seven for Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He then traveled in person through the Nine Border Regions from Jiangbei and submitted one set of colony reforms after another: four for Jiangbei, nine for Jizhen, eleven each for Liaodong and Xuan-Da, four for Ningxia, and seven for Gansu.

sentences.zh: 奏輒報可。

translations.literal: Whenever he submitted a memorial, approval was promptly returned.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials were approved as soon as they arrived.

sentences.zh: 尚鵬權既重，自負經濟才，慷慨任事。

translations.literal: Shangpeng's authority was now great; confident in his talent for statecraft, he served with bold dedication.
translations.idiomatic: With his authority greatly expanded, Shangpeng, confident in his talent for practical administration, threw himself into his duties with bold energy.

sentences.zh: 諸御史督鹽政者以事權見奪，欲攻去之。

translations.literal: The censors who supervised salt administration, seeing their authority taken away, sought to drive him out.
translations.idiomatic: The censors charged with overseeing salt policy, finding their power curtailed, tried to force him out.

sentences.zh: 河東巡鹽郜永春劾尚鵬行事乖違，吏部尚書楊博議留之。

translations.literal: Gao Yongchun, inspector of salt in Hedong, impeached Shangpeng for irregular conduct; Minister of Personnel Yang Bo argued that he should be retained.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yongchun, the Hedong salt inspector, impeached Shangpeng for misconduct, but Minister of Personnel Yang Bo argued that he should be kept in office.

sentences.zh: 會中官惡博，激帝怒，譙讓，罷博而落尚鵬職，汰屯鹽都御史官。

translations.literal: It happened that palace eunuchs hated Bo; they stirred the emperor's anger, and after rebuke and reproach Bo was dismissed, Shangpeng was removed from office, and the post of censor-in-chief over colonies and salt was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs who hated Bo provoked the emperor's wrath; after a sharp rebuke Bo was dismissed, Shangpeng was stripped of his post, and the office of censor-in-chief over colonies and salt was abolished altogether.

sentences.zh: 時三年十二月也。

translations.literal: This was in the twelfth month of the third year.
translations.idiomatic: This took place in the twelfth month of the third year.

sentences.zh: 明年，復坐按浙時驗進宮幣不中程，斥為民。

translations.literal: The following year he was again punished because, while inspecting Zhejiang, the tribute silks he had certified for the palace failed to meet the required standard, and he was dismissed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was punished again: while serving as inspector in Zhejiang, the palace silks he had certified had failed to meet standard, and he was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，御史計坤亨等交薦，保定巡撫宋纁亦白其無罪。

translations.literal: When the Shenzong Emperor ascended the throne, Censor Ji Kunheng and others jointly recommended him, and Song Li, grand coordinator of Baoding, also declared him innocent.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shenzong Emperor came to the throne, Censor Ji Kunheng and others recommended him in turn, and Song Li, grand coordinator of Baoding, also testified to his innocence.

sentences.zh: 萬曆四年冬，始以故官撫福建。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Wanli he was at last appointed grand coordinator of Fujian with his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Wanli 4 he was at last restored to his former rank and made grand coordinator of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 奏蠲逋餉銀，推行一條鞭法。

translations.literal: He memorialized to remit overdue tax silver and implemented the Single Whip Method.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for the remission of overdue tax payments and introduced the Single Whip Method of taxation.

sentences.zh: 劾罷總兵官胡守仁，屬吏咸奉職。

translations.literal: He impeached and removed the regional commander Hu Shouren, and all subordinate officials thereafter performed their duties properly.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached and dismissed the regional commander Hu Shouren, after which all his subordinates performed their duties as they should.

sentences.zh: 張居正奪情，重譴言者。

translations.literal: When Zhang Juzheng sought to retain office during mourning, those who spoke against it were heavily punished.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng sought to remain in office rather than observe mourning, those who objected were punished severely.

sentences.zh: 尚鵬移書救，居正深銜之。

translations.literal: Shangpeng sent a letter pleading on their behalf, and Juzheng deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Shangpeng wrote in their defense, and Juzheng took deep offense.

sentences.zh: 會拜左副都御史，居正令吏科陳三謨以給由歲月有誤劾之，遂罷去。

translations.literal: Just as he was appointed Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, Juzheng had Chen Sanmo of the Ministry of Personnel section impeach him on the grounds of an error in the dates on his appointment document, and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When he was appointed Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, Juzheng had Chen Sanmo of the Ministry of Personnel section impeach him over a mistake in the dates on his appointment papers, and he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 家居四年卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home for four years and then died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for four years and then died.

sentences.zh: 浙江、福建暨其鄉廣東皆以徭輕故德尚鵬，立祠祀。

translations.literal: Zhejiang, Fujian, and his native Guangdong all honored Shangpeng because corvée burdens had been lightened under him, and temples were erected to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Zhejiang, Fujian, and his native Guangdong all revered Shangpeng for the lighter corvée burdens he had brought them, and erected temples in his honor.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，賜謚惠敏。

translations.literal: During the Tianqi reign he was posthumously granted the posthumous name Huimin.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign he was posthumously granted the temple name Huimin.

sentences.zh: 宋儀望，字望之，吉安永豐人。

translations.literal: Song Yiwang, style Wangzhi, was a native of Yongfeng in Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yiwang, styled Wangzhi, came from Yongfeng in Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十六年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-sixth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授吳縣知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Wu County.

sentences.zh: 民輸白糧京師，輒破家。

translations.literal: When the people delivered white grain to the capital, they were often ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Delivering tribute grain to the capital routinely ruined local households.

sentences.zh: 儀望令諸區各出公田，計役授田贍之。

translations.literal: Yiwang ordered each district to contribute public fields and, calculating labor obligations, assigned fields to support the carriers.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwang had each district set aside public fields and, according to labor quotas, assign land to support those who carried the grain.

sentences.zh: 禁火葬，創子遊祠，建書院，惠績甚著。

translations.literal: He forbade cremation, founded a Ziyou Shrine, built an academy, and his benevolent achievements were very notable.
translations.idiomatic: He banned cremation, founded the Ziyou Shrine, established an academy, and won wide renown for his benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 征授御史。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital and appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 劾大將軍仇鸞挾寇自重，疏留中。

translations.literal: He impeached the great general Qiu Luan for using the enemy to aggrandize himself; the memorial was kept at court.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached the great general Qiu Luan for using the threat of the enemy to build his own power; the memorial was shelved at court.

sentences.zh: 已，陳時務十二策。

translations.literal: Later he presented twelve policies on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He later submitted twelve proposals on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 巡鹽河東，請開桑乾河通宣、大餉道，言：「河發源金龍池下甕城驛古定橋，會眾水，東流千餘里，入盧溝橋。

translations.literal: While inspecting salt in Hedong, he requested that the Sanggan River be opened to serve as a supply route to Xuan and Da, saying: "The river rises below Jinlong Pool at the Guding Bridge by Wengcheng Post Station, gathers many streams, flows east for more than a thousand li, and enters the Lugou Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting salt in Hedong, he asked that the Sanggan River be opened as a supply route to Xuanfu and Datong, saying: "The river rises below Jinlong Pool at Guding Bridge by Wengcheng Station, gathers tributary streams, flows east for more than a thousand li, and reaches the Lugou Bridge.

sentences.zh: 其間惟大同卜村有叢石，宣府黑龍灣石崖稍險，然不逾五十里，水淺者猶二三尺，疏鑿甚易。

translations.literal: Along its course only Bucun in Datong has clustered rocks, and the stone cliffs at Heilongwan in Xuanfu are somewhat steep, yet this extends no more than fifty li; where the water is shallow it is still two or three chi deep, and dredging would be very easy.
translations.idiomatic: Along the way only Bucun in Datong has clustered rocks, and the stone cliffs at Heilongwan in Xuanfu are somewhat steep, yet this stretch is no more than fifty li; even in the shallowest places the water is still two or three chi deep, and dredging would be easy.

sentences.zh: 曩大同巡撫侯鉞嘗乘小艇赴懷來，歷卜村、黑龍灣，安行無虞。

translations.literal: Formerly Hou Yue, grand coordinator of Datong, once took a small boat to Huailai, passing through Bucun and Heilongwan, and traveled safely without incident.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Hou Yue, grand coordinator of Datong, had taken a small boat to Huailai by way of Bucun and Heilongwan and traveled safely without trouble.

sentences.zh: 又自懷來溯流，載米三十石達之古定河，足利漕可徵。

translations.literal: He also went upstream from Huailai and transported thirty shi of grain to Guding River, showing that the benefits of grain transport could indeed be realized.
translations.idiomatic: He also went upstream from Huailai and carried thirty shi of grain as far as Guding River, proving that the route could profitably be used for grain transport.

sentences.zh: 」時方行挖運，率三十石致一石。

translations.literal: " At that time the overland transport method was in use, and on average thirty shi had to be dispatched to deliver one shi.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time overland transport was in use, and it took roughly thirty shi dispatched to deliver one shi to its destination.

sentences.zh: 儀望疏至，下廷議。

translations.literal: When Yiwang's memorial arrived, it was sent down for court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When Yiwang's memorial arrived, the court referred it for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書聶豹言：「河成便漕，兼制敵騎。

translations.literal: Minister of War Nie Bao said: "If the river is completed, transport will be convenient and enemy cavalry can also be contained.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Nie Bao said: "Once the river is opened, transport will be easier and enemy cavalry can be contained as well.

sentences.zh: 」工部尚書歐陽必進言：「道遠役重。

translations.literal: " Minister of Works Ouyang Bijin said: "The route is long and the labor burden heavy.
translations.idiomatic: " Minister of Works Ouyang Bijin said: "The route is too long and the labor burden too heavy.

sentences.zh: 」遂報罷。

translations.literal: " The proposal was then rejected.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 儀望尋省母歸。

translations.literal: Yiwang soon returned home to visit his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwang soon went home on leave to visit his mother.

sentences.zh: 還朝，發胡宗憲、阮鶚奸貪狀，鶚被逮。

translations.literal: On returning to court, he exposed the corruption of Hu Zongxian and Ruan E; E was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to court, he exposed the corruption of Hu Zongxian and Ruan E, and E was arrested.

sentences.zh: 二人皆嚴嵩私人，嵩由是不悅。

translations.literal: Both men were private associates of Yan Song, and Song was displeased on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Both were protégés of Yan Song, who was displeased by the attack.

sentences.zh: 及受命督三殿門工，嵩子世蕃私賈人金，屬必進俾與工事，儀望執不可。

translations.literal: When he was ordered to supervise work on the gates of the Three Halls, Song's son Shifan privately accepted money from merchants and asked Bijin to assign them to the project; Yiwang firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: When he was assigned to supervise work on the gates of the Three Halls, Song's son Shifan had secretly taken money from merchants and asked Bijin to put them on the project; Yiwang refused.

sentences.zh: 工竣，敘勞，擢大理右寺丞。

translations.literal: When the work was completed, merits were recorded and he was promoted to Right Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, rewards were distributed and he was promoted to Right Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 世蕃以為德，儀望請急歸，無所謝，世蕃益怒。

translations.literal: Shifan regarded this as a favor, but Yiwang requested urgent leave to return home and offered no thanks; Shifan grew all the more angry.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan took this as a personal favor, but Yiwang asked for urgent leave to go home and offered no thanks, which made Shifan angrier still.

sentences.zh: 會災異考察京官，必進遷吏部，遂坐以浮躁，貶夷陵判官。

translations.literal: When an evaluation of capital officials was conducted on account of calamities and portents, Bijin was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and Yiwang was punished for being frivolous and demoted to assistant magistrate of Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: During an evaluation of capital officials prompted by omens and disasters, Bijin was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and Yiwang was found frivolous and demoted to assistant magistrate of Yiling.

sentences.zh: 嵩敗，擢霸州兵備僉事。

translations.literal: When Song fell, Yiwang was promoted to military intendant of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Song's downfall he was promoted to military intendant of Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 請城涿州，除馬戶逋稅。

translations.literal: He requested that Zhuozhou be fortified and overdue taxes owed by horse households be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Zhuozhou be fortified and that overdue taxes owed by horse-rearing households be remitted.

sentences.zh: 進大名兵備副使，改福建。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice commissioner of military preparedness in Daming and then transferred to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commissioner of military preparedness in Daming and then transferred to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 與總兵官戚繼光合兵破倭，因列海防善後事。

translations.literal: Together with regional commander Qi Jiguang he combined forces and defeated the pirates, then set forth measures for follow-up coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: He joined regional commander Qi Jiguang in defeating the pirates and then laid out plans for strengthening coastal defense afterward.

sentences.zh: 詔從其請。

translations.literal: An edict approved his request.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved his proposals.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年，吏部尚書楊博欲黜儀望，考功郎劉一儒持之，乃鐫二秩，補四川僉事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longqing, Minister of Personnel Yang Bo wished to dismiss Yiwang, but Merit Evaluation Officer Liu Yiru defended him; Yiwang was instead reduced two ranks and appointed assistant commissioner in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 2, Minister of Personnel Yang Bo wanted to dismiss Yiwang, but Merit Evaluation Officer Liu Yiru defended him; Yiwang was reduced two ranks instead and appointed assistant commissioner in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 四遷大理少卿。

translations.literal: After four promotions he became Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: After four promotions he rose to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二年，張居正當國，雅知儀望才，擢右僉都御史，巡撫應天諸府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wanli, when Zhang Juzheng held power, he had long known Yiwang's talent and promoted him to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief as grand coordinator of the prefectures of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 2, with Zhang Juzheng in power, he promoted Yiwang, whose ability he had long respected, to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of the Yingtian prefectures.

sentences.zh: 奏減屬郡災賦。

translations.literal: He memorialized to reduce disaster taxes in the subordinate prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for reduced disaster levies in the subordinate prefectures.

sentences.zh: 海警稍定，將吏諱言兵，儀望與副使王叔果修戰備。

translations.literal: As coastal alarms subsided, officers avoided speaking of military matters; Yiwang and Vice Commissioner Wang Shuguo repaired war preparations.
translations.idiomatic: As coastal alarms eased, officers avoided discussing military matters, but Yiwang and Vice Commissioner Wang Shuguo set about restoring defenses.

sentences.zh: 倭果至，禦之黑水洋，斬獲多，進右副都御史。

translations.literal: The pirates did arrive; he met them at Heishuiyang, killed and captured many, and was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The pirates did come; he fought them at Heishuiyang, killed and captured many, and was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 先有詔雪建文諸臣，儀望創表忠祠祀之南京。

translations.literal: There had earlier been an edict rehabilitating the ministers of the Jianwen reign; Yiwang founded the Biaozhong Shrine in Nanjing to worship them.
translations.idiomatic: After an earlier edict had rehabilitated the ministers who served the Jianwen Emperor, Yiwang founded the Shrine of Loyalty in Nanjing to honor them.

sentences.zh: 宋忠臣楊邦晙，儀望鄉人也，葬江寧，歲久漸湮，儀望為封其墓，載其祠祀典。

translations.literal: The Song loyalist Yang Bangjun, a townsman of Yiwang, was buried in Jiangning; after many years the grave was gradually lost, and Yiwang had the tomb restored and entered his worship in the ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: The Song loyalist Yang Bangjun, a fellow townsman of Yiwang, was buried in Jiangning; after years the grave had fallen into neglect, and Yiwang restored the tomb and had his worship entered in the state ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 故太常卿袁洪愈、祭酒姜寶皆不為居正所喜，儀望薦之朝，漸失居正意。

translations.literal: The former Director of Ceremonies Yuan Hongyu and the Chancellor of the National Academy Jiang Bao were both disliked by Juzheng; Yiwang recommended them at court and gradually lost Juzheng's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Former Director of Ceremonies Yuan Hongyu and National Academy Chancellor Jiang Bao were both out of Juzheng's favor; when Yiwang recommended them at court he gradually lost Juzheng's goodwill.

sentences.zh: 四年，稍遷南京大理卿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was gradually transferred to Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to Chief Minister of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 逾年改北，被劾罷歸。

translations.literal: The following year he was transferred to the northern capital, was impeached, dismissed, and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to Beijing, was impeached, dismissed, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 儀望少師聶豹，私淑王守仁，又從鄒守益、歐陽德、羅洪先遊。

translations.literal: Yiwang studied under Nie Bao in his youth, privately admired Wang Shouren, and also associated with Zou Shouyi, Ouyang De, and Luo Hongxian.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yiwang studied under Nie Bao, privately admired Wang Shouren, and also learned from Zou Shouyi, Ouyang De, and Luo Hongxian.

sentences.zh: 守仁從祀，儀望有力焉。

translations.literal: When Shouren was granted posthumous worship in the temple, Yiwang had contributed significantly.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwang had played a major part in securing posthumous worship for Shouren in the Confucian temple.

sentences.zh: 家居數年卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home for several years and then died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for several years and then died.

sentences.zh: 張嶽，字汝宗，餘姚人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue, style Ruzong, was a native of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue, styled Ruzong, came from Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十八年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-eighth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed palace courier.

sentences.zh: 擢禮科給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Rites section.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Rites section.

sentences.zh: 巡視內府庫藏，奏行厘弊八事。

translations.literal: While inspecting the inner palace storehouses, he memorialized and implemented eight measures to rectify abuses.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting the inner palace storehouses, he memorialized eight measures to rectify abuses and had them carried out.

sentences.zh: 已，又陳時政，極言講學者以富貴功名鼓動士大夫，談虛論寂，靡然成風。

translations.literal: Later he also addressed current policy, saying at length that lecturers stirred officials with wealth, rank, and fame, and that empty talk of quietism had become a prevailing fashion.
translations.idiomatic: He later addressed current affairs as well, arguing at length that lecturers were stirring officials with promises of wealth and rank and that empty talk of quietism had become a widespread fashion.

sentences.zh: 又今吏治方清，獨兵部無振刷，推用總兵黃印、韓承慶等，非庸即狡。

translations.literal: He also said that while civil administration was now being cleaned up, the Ministry of War alone had not been revitalized, and the regional commanders it promoted, such as Huang Yin and Han Chengqing, were either mediocre or cunning.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that while civil administration was being cleaned up, the Ministry of War alone had not been revived, and the regional commanders it promoted, such as Huang Yin and Han Chengqing, were either mediocre or cunning.

sentences.zh: 曹司條例淆亂無章，胥吏朋奸，搏噬將校，其咎必有所歸。

translations.literal: Department regulations were confused and without order; clerks formed factions to commit fraud and prey on officers, and blame for this must rest somewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Department regulations were chaotic and disordered; clerks formed factions to commit fraud and prey on officers, and someone had to be held responsible.

sentences.zh: 時徐階當國，為講學會，而楊博在兵部，意蓋指二人也。

translations.literal: At the time Xu Jie held power and led lecture gatherings, while Yang Bo was in the Ministry of War; his meaning was clearly aimed at the two of them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xu Jie held power and led lecture gatherings, while Yang Bo headed the Ministry of War; he clearly had the two of them in mind.

sentences.zh: 博奏辨乞罷，帝慰留之。

translations.literal: Bo memorialized in defense and asked to resign; the emperor comforted him and kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: Bo memorialized in his defense and asked to resign; the emperor reassured him and kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 博自是惡嶽。

translations.literal: From then on Bo hated Yue.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Bo hated Yue.

sentences.zh: 及掌吏部，嶽已遷工科左給事中，遂出為雲南參議。

translations.literal: When he took charge of the Ministry of Personnel, Yue had already been transferred to Left Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of Works section, and was then sent out as administrative vice commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Bo took charge of the Ministry of Personnel, Yue had already been transferred to Left Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of Works section and was then sent out as administrative vice commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 再遷河南參政。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to administrative commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to administrative commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，張居正雅知嶽，用為太僕少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli, Zhang Juzheng, who had long known Yue's worth, appointed him Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign Zhang Juzheng, who had long respected Yue's ability, appointed him Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 再遷南京右僉都御史，督操江。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief in Nanjing to supervise the Caojiang defense force.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief in Nanjing to supervise the Yangtze defense force.

sentences.zh: 甫到官，會居正父喪謀奪情，南京尚書潘晟及諸給事、御史，咸上疏請留居正。

translations.literal: He had barely taken office when Juzheng, upon his father's death, sought to retain office during mourning; Minister Pan Sheng of Nanjing and the supervising secretaries and censors all submitted memorials asking that Juzheng be kept in post.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely taken office when Juzheng, mourning his father's death, sought to remain in office; Minister Pan Sheng of Nanjing and the supervising secretaries and censors all memorialized asking that Juzheng be kept at his post.

sentences.zh: 嶽獨馳疏請令馳驛奔喪，居正大怒。

translations.literal: Yue alone sent an urgent memorial asking that Juzheng be ordered to travel by post relay to observe mourning; Juzheng was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: Yue alone sent an urgent memorial asking that Juzheng be ordered to travel by post relay to observe mourning, and Juzheng was furious.

sentences.zh: 會大計京官，給事中傅作舟等承風劾嶽，貶一秩調外，嶽遂歸。

translations.literal: When the grand evaluation of capital officials took place, Supervising Secretary Fu Zuozhou and others, following the prevailing wind, impeached Yue; he was demoted one rank and transferred outside the capital, and Yue returned home.
translations.idiomatic: During the grand evaluation of capital officials, Supervising Secretary Fu Zuozhou and others, taking their cue from the prevailing mood, impeached Yue; he was demoted one rank and transferred outside the capital, and Yue went home.

sentences.zh: 久之，操江僉都御史呂藿、給事中吳綰知居正憾未釋，摭劾嶽落職閑住。

translations.literal: After some time, Caojiang Assistant Censor-in-Chief Lü Huo and Supervising Secretary Wu Wan, knowing that Juzheng's resentment had not yet subsided, gathered charges to impeach Yue and have him dismissed to idle residence.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later, Yangtze defense Assistant Censor-in-Chief Lü Huo and Supervising Secretary Wu Wan, knowing Juzheng's resentment had not faded, gathered charges against Yue and had him dismissed to idle residence.

sentences.zh: 甫兩月，居正死，南京御史方萬山薦嶽，劾作舟。

translations.literal: After only two months Juzheng died; Nanjing Censor Fang Wanshan recommended Yue and impeached Zuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Barely two months later Juzheng died; Nanjing Censor Fang Wanshan recommended Yue and impeached Zuozhou.

sentences.zh: 作舟坐斥，起嶽四川參議。

translations.literal: Zuozhou was dismissed on the charge, and Yue was recalled as administrative vice commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zuozhou was dismissed, and Yue was recalled as administrative vice commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 旋擢右僉都御史，巡撫南、贛。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief as grand coordinator of Nan and Gan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of Nan and Gan.

sentences.zh: 入為左僉都御史，獻時政四議。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief and presented four proposals on current policy.
translations.idiomatic: He was brought into the capital as Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief and submitted four proposals on current policy.

sentences.zh: 其一言宗藩宜以世次遞殺，親盡則停，俾習四民之業。

translations.literal: One said that imperial clansmen should be reduced in rank by generation in succession, and when kinship was exhausted the reduction should stop, so that they might practice the occupations of the four classes of people.
translations.idiomatic: One argued that imperial clansmen should be reduced in rank generation by generation, stopping when the degree of kinship was exhausted, so that they might take up the ordinary occupations of common people.

sentences.zh: 其一言治河之策，夏鎮固當開，沽頭亦不可廢。

translations.literal: Another spoke on river-control policy: Xiazhen should indeed be opened, but Gutou should not be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Another addressed river-control policy: Xiazhen should indeed be opened, but Gutou should not be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 並報寢。

translations.literal: Both were reported shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were shelved.

sentences.zh: 進左副都御史，上疏評議廷臣賢否，為給事中袁國臣等所論。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and submitted a memorial evaluating whether court officials were worthy or not; he was impeached by Supervising Secretary Yuan Guochen and others.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and submitted a memorial assessing which court officials were worthy and which were not; Supervising Secretary Yuan Guochen and others impeached him for it.

sentences.zh: 時已遷刑部右侍郎，坐罷歸。

translations.literal: By then he had already been transferred to Right Vice Minister of Justice; on this charge he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had already been transferred to Right Vice Minister of Justice; on this charge he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 李材，字孟誠，豐城人，尚書遂子也。

translations.literal: Li Cai, style Mengcheng, was a native of Fengcheng and the son of Minister Li Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cai, styled Mengcheng, came from Fengcheng and was the son of Minister Li Sui.

sentences.zh: 舉嘉靖四十一年進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-first year of Jiajing and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-first year of the Jiajing reign and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 素從鄒守益講學。

translations.literal: He had long followed Zou Shouyi in the study of learning.
translations.idiomatic: He had long studied under Zou Shouyi.

sentences.zh: 自以學未成，乞假歸。

translations.literal: Considering his learning still incomplete, he requested leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Believing his studies were not yet finished, he asked for leave to go home.

sentences.zh: 訪唐樞、王畿、錢德洪，與問難。

translations.literal: He visited Tang Shu, Wang Ji, and Qian Dehong and engaged in questioning and debate with them.
translations.idiomatic: He visited Tang Shu, Wang Ji, and Qian Dehong and debated with them.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中還朝。

translations.literal: During the Longqing reign he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longqing reign he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 由兵部郎中稍遷廣東僉事。

translations.literal: From his post as a director in the Ministry of War he was gradually promoted to vice commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a director in the Ministry of War, he was gradually promoted to vice commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 羅旁賊猖獗，材襲破之周高山，設屯以守。

translations.literal: The Luopang bandits were rampant; Cai launched a surprise attack and defeated them at Zhougao Mountain and established garrison colonies to hold the place.
translations.idiomatic: When the Luopang bandits grew bold, Cai routed them in a surprise attack at Zhougao Mountain and set up garrison colonies to hold the area.

sentences.zh: 賊有三巢在新會境，調副總兵梁守愚由恩平，遊擊王瑞由德慶入，身出肇慶中道，夜半斬賊五百級，毀廬舍千餘，空其地，募人田之。

translations.literal: The bandits had three lairs within Xinhui territory; Cai dispatched Vice Regional Commander Liang Shouyu to enter from Enping and Mobile Corps Commander Wang Rui from Deqing, while he himself advanced from Zhaoqing along the middle route; at midnight they killed five hundred bandits, destroyed more than a thousand dwellings, cleared the land, and recruited people to farm it.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits maintained three strongholds in Xinhui. Cai sent Vice Regional Commander Liang Shouyu in from Enping and Mobile Corps Commander Wang Rui from Deqing, while he himself marched from Zhaoqing along the central route. At midnight they killed five hundred bandits, destroyed over a thousand dwellings, emptied the territory, and recruited settlers to farm the land.

sentences.zh: 亡何，倭五千攻陷電白，大掠而去。

translations.literal: Before long, five thousand Wokou attacked and captured Dianbai, looted heavily, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, five thousand Japanese pirates attacked and seized Dianbai, plundered the region, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 材追破之石城，設伏海口，伺其遁而殲之，奪還婦女三千餘。

translations.literal: Cai pursued and defeated them at Shicheng, set an ambush at Haikou, waited for their retreat and annihilated them, and recovered more than three thousand women.
translations.idiomatic: Cai pursued them, defeated them at Shicheng, and laid an ambush at Haikou. When they fled, he wiped them out and recovered more than three thousand captive women.

sentences.zh: 會奸人引倭自黃山間道潰而東。

translations.literal: It happened that treacherous men guided the Wokou along a bypath at Huangshan to break through and flee eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Traitors then guided the pirates along a hidden route through Huangshan, and they broke out and fled east.

sentences.zh: 材聲言大軍數道至以疑賊，而返故道迎擊，盡殺之。

translations.literal: Cai proclaimed that large armies were arriving on several routes to confuse the bandits, then returned along the original path to intercept them and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Cai spread word that large forces were converging from several directions to unsettle the enemy, then doubled back along the original route to intercept them and killed them to the last man.

sentences.zh: 又追襲雷州倭至英利，皆遁去，降賊渠許恩於陽江。

translations.literal: He also pursued the Leizhou Wokou to Yingli; they all fled, and the bandit chieftain Xu En surrendered at Yangjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He also pursued the Leizhou pirates as far as Yingli; they all escaped, and the bandit leader Xu En surrendered at Yangjiang.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進副使。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was promoted to vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were recognized and he was promoted to vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，張居正柄國，不悅材，遂引疾去。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli, Zhang Juzheng held power; displeased with Cai, Cai cited illness and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign, Zhang Juzheng dominated the government. Unhappy with Cai, Juzheng drove him out on the pretext of illness.

sentences.zh: 居正卒，起官山東。

translations.literal: After Juzheng died, Cai was recalled to serve in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng's death, Cai was recalled to office in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 以才調遼東開原。

translations.literal: On account of his ability he was transferred to Kaiyuan in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Recognizing his talent, the court transferred him to Kaiyuan in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 尋遷雲南洱海參政，進按察使，備兵金騰。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to administrative commissioner of Erhai in Yunnan, promoted to surveillance commissioner, and charged with military affairs at Jinteng.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made administrative commissioner of Erhai in Yunnan, then promoted to surveillance commissioner with responsibility for military affairs at Jinteng.

sentences.zh: 金騰地接緬甸，而孟養、蠻莫兩土司介其間，叛服不常。

translations.literal: The Jinteng region bordered Burma, with the two native chieftaincies of Mengyang and Manmo lying between them; their submission and rebellion were inconstant.
translations.idiomatic: Jinteng bordered Burma, with the Mengyang and Manmo chieftaincies lying between them—tribes whose loyalty shifted unpredictably.

sentences.zh: 緬部目曰大曩長、曰散奪者，率數千人據其地。

translations.literal: Burmese chiefs named Da Nangchang and San Duo led several thousand men in occupying the territory.
translations.idiomatic: Two Burmese chiefs, Da Nangchang and San Duo, led several thousand men in seizing the area.

sentences.zh: 材謂不收兩土司無以制緬，遣人招兩土司來歸，而間討抗命夷阿坡。

translations.literal: Cai said that without winning back the two chieftaincies there would be no means of restraining Burma; he sent men to summon both chieftaincies to submit, while meanwhile attacking the recalcitrant tribesman A Po.
translations.idiomatic: Cai argued that without bringing the two chieftaincies back into allegiance he could not control Burma. He sent envoys to win them over while quietly moving against the defiant tribesman A Po.

sentences.zh: 居頃之，緬遣兵爭蠻莫，材合兩土司兵敗緬眾，殺大曩長，逐散奪去。

translations.literal: Before long Burma sent troops to contest Manmo; Cai combined the forces of the two chieftaincies and defeated the Burmese, killed Da Nangchang, and drove San Duo away.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Burma sent troops to seize Manmo. Cai joined forces with the two chieftaincies, routed the Burmese army, killed Da Nangchang, and drove San Duo off.

sentences.zh: 緬帥莽應裏益兵至孟養，復擊沈其舟，斬其將一人，乃退。

translations.literal: The Burmese commander Mang Yingli reinforced his troops and advanced to Mengyang; Cai again attacked, sank their boats, beheaded one of their generals, and then they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese commander Mang Yingli reinforced his army and marched on Mengyang. Cai attacked again, sank their boats, killed one of their generals, and forced them to retreat.

sentences.zh: 有猛密者，地在緬境，數為緬侵奪，舉族內徙，有司居之戶碗。

translations.literal: There was a place called Mengmi, lying within Burmese territory, which had repeatedly been seized by Burma; the whole clan moved inward, and the local authorities resettled them at Huwan.
translations.idiomatic: Mengmi lay within Burmese territory and had been repeatedly overrun by Burma. Its people migrated en masse inland, and the local authorities resettled them at Huwan.

sentences.zh: 至是，緬勢稍屈，材資遣還故土。

translations.literal: At this time Burmese power had weakened somewhat, and Cai provided funds to send them back to their original lands.
translations.idiomatic: By then Burmese strength had waned, and Cai supplied funds to help them return to their homeland.

sentences.zh: 亡何，緬人驅象陣大舉復仇，兩土司告急。

translations.literal: Before long the Burmese drove elephant formations in a major campaign of revenge, and the two chieftaincies sent urgent appeals for help.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Burmese launched a massive counterattack with elephant formations, and both chieftaincies sent desperate appeals for aid.

sentences.zh: 材遣遊擊劉天俸率把總寇崇德等出威緬，渡金沙江，與孟養兵會遮浪，迎擊之。

translations.literal: Cai dispatched Mobile Corps Commander Liu Tianfeng, leading petty officers Kou Chongde and others, out through Weimian, crossed the Jinsha River, joined Mengyang troops at Zhelang, and met the enemy in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Cai sent Mobile Corps Commander Liu Tianfeng with petty officers including Kou Chongde out through Weimian. They crossed the Jinsha River, joined Mengyang forces at Zhelang, and engaged the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賊大敗，生擒繡衣賊將三人。

translations.literal: The enemy was routed; three enemy generals in embroidered robes were captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy suffered a crushing defeat, and three of their generals in embroidered robes were taken alive.

sentences.zh: 巡撫劉世曾、總兵官沐昌祚以大捷聞，詔令覆勘。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Liu Shizeng and Regional Commander Mu Changzuo reported a great victory; an edict ordered a review of the claims.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Liu Shizeng and Regional Commander Mu Changzuo reported a great victory to the throne, and the emperor ordered an independent review of their claims.

sentences.zh: 未上，而材擢右僉都御史，撫治鄖陽。

translations.literal: Before the report was submitted, Cai was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before the review could be completed, Cai was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and appointed grand coordinator of Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 材好講學，遣部卒供生徒役，卒多怨。

translations.literal: Cai loved to lecture on learning and had his subordinate soldiers serve as labor for his students; the soldiers resented this greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Cai was devoted to teaching and assigned his soldiers to wait on his students; the troops deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 又徇諸生請，改參將公署為學宮。

translations.literal: He also acceded to the students' request and converted the brigade commander's official residence into a school.
translations.idiomatic: At the students' urging, he also converted the brigade commander's headquarters into a school.

sentences.zh: 參將米萬春諷門卒梅林等大噪，馳入城，縱囚毀諸生廬，直趨軍門，挾賞銀四千，洶洶不解。

translations.literal: Brigade Commander Mi Wanchun incited the gate soldiers Mei Lin and others to raise a loud uproar; they galloped into the city, released prisoners, destroyed the students' quarters, marched straight to headquarters, and demanded four thousand taels of silver in rewards, remaining in a tumultuous standoff.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade Commander Mi Wanchun goaded gate soldiers led by Mei Lin into a riot. They galloped into the city, freed prisoners, wrecked the students' lodgings, marched on headquarters, and demanded four thousand taels in reward money, refusing to disperse.

sentences.zh: 居二日，萬春脅材更軍中不便十二事，令上疏歸罪副使丁惟寧、知府沈鈇等，材隱忍從之。

translations.literal: After two days, Wanchun coerced Cai to revise twelve troublesome military matters and submit a memorial placing blame on Vice Commissioner Ding Weining, Prefect Shen Fu, and others; Cai endured it and complied.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later, Wanchun forced Cai to alter twelve disputed military regulations and submit a memorial blaming Vice Commissioner Ding Weining, Prefect Shen Fu, and others. Cai swallowed his pride and agreed.

sentences.zh: 惟寧責數萬春，萬春欲殺惟寧，跳而免，材遂復劾惟寧激變。

translations.literal: Weining rebuked Wanchun repeatedly; Wanchun wished to kill Weining, who leaped away and escaped; Cai then again impeached Weining for inciting the mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Weining sharply rebuked Wanchun, who tried to kill him; Weining leaped aside and escaped. Cai then impeached Weining again, accusing him of provoking the mutiny.

sentences.zh: 詔下鈇等吏，貶惟寧三官，材還籍候勘。

translations.literal: An edict sent Fu and others to the courts for trial, degraded Weining by three ranks, and ordered Cai to return to his native place pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred Shen Fu and the others to the courts, demoted Weining by three ranks, and sent Cai home to await investigation.

sentences.zh: 時十五年十一月也。

translations.literal: This was in the eleventh month of the fifteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: This occurred in the eleventh month of Wanli 15.

sentences.zh: 御史楊紹程勘萬春首亂，宜罪。

translations.literal: Censor Yang Shaocheng investigated and found that Wanchun had initiated the mutiny and should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yang Shaocheng investigated the affair and concluded that Wanchun had started the riot and deserved punishment.

sentences.zh: 大學士申時行庇之，置不問，旋調天津善地去。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shen Shihang shielded him, took no action, and soon transferred him to a comfortable post in Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shen Shihang protected him, let the matter drop, and soon transferred him to a soft appointment in Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 而材又以雲南事被訐，遂獲重譴。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Cai was again denounced over the Yunnan affair and thus received severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Cai was then denounced again over the Yunnan campaign and suffered heavy punishment.

sentences.zh: 初，有詔勘征緬功，巡按御史蘇贊阝言斬馘不及千，破城拓地皆無驗，猛密地尚為緬據，材、天俸等虛張功伐，副使陳嚴之與相附和，宜並罪。

translations.literal: Earlier, an edict had been issued to investigate the achievements in the campaign against Burma; Investigating Censor Su Zan stated that decapitated heads numbered fewer than a thousand, that captures of cities and expansion of territory were all unverified, that Mengmi was still held by the Burmese, that Cai, Tianfeng, and others had inflated their accomplishments, that Vice Commissioner Chen Yanzhi had echoed them, and that all should be punished together.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the throne had ordered an inquiry into the Burma campaign. Investigating Censor Su Zan reported that fewer than a thousand heads had been taken, that no city captures or territorial gains could be verified, that Mengmi remained in Burmese hands, and that Cai, Tianfeng, and others had exaggerated their achievements—with Vice Commissioner Chen Yanzhi backing their claims. He argued that all should be punished.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，削世曾籍，奪昌祚祿一年，材、嚴之、天俸俱逮下詔獄。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged; Shizeng was stripped of his rank, Changzuo was deprived of salary for one year, and Cai, Yanzhi, and Tianfeng were all arrested and sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage. Shizeng was stripped of rank, Changzuo lost a year's salary, and Cai, Yanzhi, and Tianfeng were all thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書李世達、左都御史吳時來、大理少卿李棟等，當材、天俸徒，嚴之鐫秩。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Li Shida, Left Censor-in-Chief Wu Shilai, Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Li Dong, and others sentenced Cai and Tianfeng to penal servitude and Yanzhi to demotion by engraved ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Li Shida, Left Censor-in-Chief Wu Shilai, Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Li Dong, and others recommended penal servitude for Cai and Tianfeng and a rank reduction for Yanzhi.

sentences.zh: 帝不懌，奪郎中、御史、寺正諸臣俸，典詔獄李登雲等亦解官。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased; he stripped the salaries of the directors, censors, and court officials involved, and Li Dengyun, superintendent of the imperial prison, and others were also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and suspended the salaries of the involved directors, censors, and court officials. Li Dengyun, who oversaw the imperial prison, and others were also removed from office.

sentences.zh: 於是改擬遣戍。

translations.literal: Thereupon the sentence was revised to exile to frontier garrison service.
translations.idiomatic: The court then revised the sentence to exile on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 特旨引紅牌說謊例，坐材、天俸斬，嚴之除名。

translations.literal: A special edict invoked the precedent on the red placard for false reporting, sentencing Cai and Tianfeng to decapitation and Yanzhi to removal from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict cited the precedent on false battle reports—the red placard case—and sentenced Cai and Tianfeng to execution while striking Yanzhi from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 大學士時行等數為解，給事中唐堯欽等亦言：「材以夷攻夷，功不可泯。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shihang and others repeatedly interceded on their behalf, and Supervising Secretary Tang Yaoqin and others also stated: "Cai used barbarians to attack barbarians; his merit cannot be erased.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shihang and others pleaded for them repeatedly, and Supervising Secretary Tang Yaoqin and others argued: "Cai used barbarians against barbarians; his achievements cannot be denied.

sentences.zh: 奏報偶虛，坐以死，假令盡虛無實，掩罪為功，何以罪之？

translations.literal: If a report is occasionally inflated, to punish with death—suppose it were entirely empty and without substance, yet crime were masked as merit: how would one punish that?
translations.idiomatic: If a battle report is occasionally exaggerated, must the penalty be death? And if reports were wholly fabricated—if failure were dressed up as victory—what punishment would be fitting then?

sentences.zh: 設不幸失城池，全軍不返，又何以罪之？

translations.literal: Suppose one were unlucky enough to lose cities and fortresses and the whole army failed to return—how would one punish that?
translations.idiomatic: And if a commander lost cities and fortresses and his entire army perished—what punishment would be fitting then?

sentences.zh: 」帝皆不聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor paid no heed to any of it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 幽系五年，論救者五十餘疏。

translations.literal: He was imprisoned in darkness for five years; more than fifty memorials pleaded for his release.
translations.idiomatic: Cai languished in prison for five years while more than fifty memorials pleaded for his release.

sentences.zh: 已，天俸以善用火器，釋令立功，時行等復為材申理，皆不省。

translations.literal: Later, Tianfeng was released on account of his skill with firearms and ordered to redeem himself through service; Shihang and others again pleaded Cai's case, but all went unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tianfeng was released because of his expertise with firearms and ordered to redeem himself in battle. Shihang and others again appealed for Cai, but the emperor would not budge.

sentences.zh: 亡何，孟養使入貢，具言緬人侵軼，天朝救援，破敵有狀，聞典兵者在獄，眾皆流涕。

translations.literal: Before long a Mengyang envoy came to pay tribute, stating in detail that the Burmese had invaded, that the celestial court had sent relief, that defeating the enemy was well attested, and that when they heard the commander was in prison, all wept.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a Mengyang tribute envoy arrived and testified in detail that the Burmese had invaded, that the court had sent relief, and that the victories were real. When they learned their commander was in prison, the whole delegation wept.

sentences.zh: 而楚雄士民閻世祥等亦相率詣闕訟冤。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the gentry and people of Chuxiong, including Yan Shixiang, also went in a body to the capital to petition for redress.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and commoners from Chuxiong, led by Yan Shixiang, also marched to the capital in a body to petition for justice.

sentences.zh: 帝意乃稍解，命再勘。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was somewhat softened, and he ordered a new investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger eased somewhat, and he ordered the case reinvestigated.

sentences.zh: 勘至，材罪不掩功。

translations.literal: When the investigation was completed, Cai's guilt did not overshadow his merit.
translations.idiomatic: The new inquiry found that Cai's faults did not outweigh his achievements.

sentences.zh: 大學士王錫爵等再疏為言，帝故遲之，至二十一年四月，始命戍鎮海衛。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Wang Xijue and others again memorialized on his behalf; the emperor deliberately delayed, until in the fourth month of the twenty-first year he finally ordered exile to the Zhenhai garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Wang Xijue and others memorialized again on his behalf, but the emperor kept delaying until the fourth month of Wanli 21, when he finally sentenced Cai to exile at the Zhenhai garrison.

sentences.zh: 材所至，輒聚徒講學，學者稱見羅先生。

translations.literal: Wherever Cai went, he would gather disciples to lecture on learning; scholars called him Master Jianluo.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Cai went, he gathered students to teach, and scholars honored him as Master Jianluo.

sentences.zh: 系獄時，就問者不絕。

translations.literal: While imprisoned, those who came to consult him never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Even in prison, students came to him without interruption.

sentences.zh: 至戍所，學徒益眾。

translations.literal: At the place of exile, his students grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: At his place of exile his following only grew.

sentences.zh: 許孚遠方巡撫福建，日相過從，材以此忘羈旅。

translations.literal: Xu Fuyuan was then grand coordinator of Fujian; they visited each other daily, and through this Cai forgot the hardship of exile.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fuyuan was then grand coordinator of Fujian, and the two visited each other daily; through his company Cai found exile bearable.

sentences.zh: 久之赦還。

translations.literal: After a long time he was pardoned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After many years he was pardoned and allowed to return home.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十九。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 陸樹德，字與成，尚書樹聲弟也。

translations.literal: Lu Shude, style Yucheng, was the younger brother of Minister Lu Shusheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shude, styled Yucheng, was the younger brother of Minister Lu Shusheng.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖末進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination at the end of the Jiajing reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the final years of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 除嚴州推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He received appointment as investigating prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 行取當授給事、御史，會樹聲拜侍郎，乃授刑部主事。

translations.literal: Selected for advancement he was to receive appointment as supervising secretary or censor, but as Shusheng had been appointed vice minister, he was instead appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Selected for promotion to the capital, he was slated for appointment as a supervising secretary or censor; but because Shusheng had become a vice minister, he was instead made a secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 隆慶四年，改禮科給事中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Longqing he was transferred to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Rites section.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 4 he was transferred to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Rites section.

sentences.zh: 穆宗御朝講，不發一語。

translations.literal: When the Muzong Emperor attended court lectures, he did not speak a single word.
translations.idiomatic: When the Muzong Emperor attended court lectures, he never uttered a word.

sentences.zh: 樹德言：「上下交為泰，今暌隔若此，何以劘君德，訓萬幾？

translations.literal: Shude said: "When upper and lower exchange freely there is peace; now there is such estrangement—how can the sovereign's virtue be cultivated, or the myriad affairs be instructed?
translations.idiomatic: Shude said: "Harmony comes when ruler and subjects communicate openly. With such distance between you, how can Your Majesty cultivate virtue or guide the affairs of state?

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 屢遷都給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to chief supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to chief supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，詔輟東宮講讀，樹德言：「自四月迄八月，為時甚遙，請非盛暑，仍御講筵。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year, an edict suspended Eastern Palace lectures; Shude said: "From the fourth month until the eighth is a very long interval; I request that when it is not the height of summer, Your Majesty still attend the lecture hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the sixth year, an edict suspended lectures for the heir apparent. Shude wrote: "From the fourth month to the eighth is too long a break. I ask that outside the hottest summer months Your Majesty continue to hold the lecture hall.

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 穆宗頗倦勤，樹德言：「日月交蝕，旱魃為災，當及時修省。

translations.literal: The Muzong Emperor grew somewhat weary of governing; Shude said: "The sun and moon are eclipsing, and drought demons are bringing disaster; Your Majesty should promptly practice self-examination.
translations.idiomatic: As the Muzong Emperor grew weary of statecraft, Shude wrote: "Solar and lunar eclipses and drought portend calamity. Your Majesty should examine yourself and reform without delay.

sentences.zh: 」及帝不豫，又請謹藥餌，善保護，仲夏亢陽月，宜益慎起居。

translations.literal: " When the emperor fell ill, he also requested care in taking medicines and proper protection; in the midsummer month of intense yang heat, one should be all the more cautious in daily conduct.
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor fell ill, Shude also urged caution with medicines and careful self-protection, noting that in the sweltering midsummer month one must be especially mindful of daily regimen.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，疏皆留中。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased; all memorials were kept at court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took offense, and his memorials were all shelved without response.

sentences.zh: 內臣請祈福戒壇，已得旨，樹德言：「戒壇度僧，男女擾雜，導淫傷化。

translations.literal: Inner court eunuchs requested a fasting altar for prayer for blessings; once approval was granted, Shude said: "At fasting altars monks are ordained, men and women mingle in disorder, leading to licentiousness and harm to moral transformation.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuchs requested a fasting altar to pray for blessings and the request was approved, Shude objected: "At such altars monks are ordained and men and women mingle freely, encouraging licentiousness and corrupting public morals.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲保聖躬，宜法大禹之惡旨酒，成湯之不邇聲色，何必奉佛。

translations.literal: Your Majesty wishes to protect the sacred person; you should follow the Great Yu's hatred of fine wine and King Cheng Tang's keeping away from music and women—why need one worship the Buddha?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wishes to preserve your health, follow the example of Yu, who despised strong drink, and Tang, who shunned music and women. Why turn to Buddhism?

sentences.zh: 」未幾，穆宗崩，神宗嗣位，中官馮保擠司禮孟沖而代之。

translations.literal: " Before long the Muzong Emperor died; the Shenzong Emperor succeeded to the throne; the eunuch Feng Bao squeezed out Director of Ceremonies Meng Chong and replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long the Muzong Emperor died and the Shenzong Emperor succeeded him. The eunuch Feng Bao ousted Director of Ceremonies Meng Chong and took his place.

sentences.zh: 樹德言：「先帝甫崩，忽傳馮保掌司禮監。

translations.literal: Shude said: "The late emperor had just died when suddenly it was announced that Feng Bao would head the Directorate of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Shude wrote: "The late emperor had barely died when word suddenly came that Feng Bao would head the Directorate of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 果先帝意，何不傳示數日前，乃在彌留後？

translations.literal: If this truly was the late emperor's wish, why was it not proclaimed several days earlier, instead only after his final illness?
translations.idiomatic: If this was truly the late emperor's wish, why was it not announced days ago, rather than only after his deathbed?

sentences.zh: 果陛下意，則哀痛方深，萬幾未御，何暇念中官？

translations.literal: If it is Your Majesty's wish, then grief is still deep and the myriad affairs are yet untended—when would there be leisure to think of eunuchs?
translations.idiomatic: If it is Your Majesty's decision, then grief is still fresh and state affairs await attention—what time is there to concern oneself with eunuchs?

sentences.zh: 」疏入，保大恨。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, Bao hated him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial reached court, Feng Bao hated him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 比議祧廟，樹德請毋祧宣宗，仍祀睿宗世室，格不行。

translations.literal: When the ancestral temple succession was under debate, Shude requested that the Xuande Emperor not be demoted and that the Ruizong imperial chamber continue to be worshipped; this was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: During debate over ancestral temple arrangements, Shude argued against demoting the Xuande Emperor and for keeping the Ruizong imperial chamber in worship, but his proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 已，極陳民運白糧之患，請領之漕臣，從之。

translations.literal: Then he set forth at length the evils of the people's transport of white grain, requesting that it be taken over by grain transport officials; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He then detailed at length the burden of white-grain transport on the people and asked that the duty be assigned to grain-transport officials; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 樹德居言職三年，疏數十上，率侃直。

translations.literal: During three years in the remonstrance office, Shude submitted dozens of memorials, generally bold and straightforward.
translations.idiomatic: In three years as a remonstrance official, Shude submitted dozens of memorials, most of them blunt and forthright.

sentences.zh: 會樹聲掌禮部，乃量遷尚寶卿。

translations.literal: When Shusheng took charge of the Ministry of Rites, Shude was correspondingly transferred to Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When Shusheng became head of the Ministry of Rites, Shude was quietly transferred to Director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 歷太常少卿，南京太僕卿，以右僉都御史巡撫山東。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing, and finally as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, grand coordinator of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to serve as Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing, and finally as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 樹德素清嚴，約束僚吏，屏絕聲伎。

translations.literal: Shude had always been pure and stern; he restrained subordinate officials and banished music and entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Shude was known for austerity and discipline; he kept his staff in line and barred music and entertainments.

sentences.zh: 山東民壯改民兵，戍薊門，隆慶末令歲輸銀二萬四千，罷其戍役。

translations.literal: The militarily fit men of Shandong were reorganized as militia to guard the Jizhou Pass; at the end of Longqing they were ordered to pay twenty-four thousand taels of silver annually in lieu of garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong's able-bodied men had been organized as militia to garrison the Jizhou Pass; at the end of the Longqing reign they were allowed to pay twenty-four thousand taels of silver annually instead of serving.

sentences.zh: 尋命增輸三萬，樹德請如河南例罷之。

translations.literal: Soon they were ordered to pay an additional thirty thousand; Shude requested that this be abolished as in the Henan precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the court ordered an additional thirty thousand taels; Shude asked that the levy be abolished, following the Henan precedent.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，而為免增輸之數。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree, but exempted them from the increased payment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to abolish it outright but waived the increase.

sentences.zh: 德府白雲湖故民田，為王所奪，後已還民，王復結中官謀復之。

translations.literal: The Baiyun Lake lands in the De princely establishment had originally been commoners' fields, seized by the prince; they had later been returned to the people, but the prince again colluded with inner court eunuchs to plot their recovery.
translations.idiomatic: The Baiyun Lake fields of the De princely establishment had once belonged to commoners before the prince seized them. Though later restored to the people, the prince now conspired with palace eunuchs to take them back.

sentences.zh: 樹德爭不得，乞休歸。

translations.literal: Shude could not prevail in the dispute and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to win the dispute, Shude resigned and returned home.

sentences.zh: 久之卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died some years later.

sentences.zh: 蕭廩，字可發，萬安人。

translations.literal: Xiao Lin, style Kefa, was a native of Wan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Lin, styled Kefa, came from Wan'an.

sentences.zh: 祖乾元，以御史劾劉瑾，廷杖下獄，終雲南副使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qianyuan, as a censor, impeached Liu Jin, was beaten at court and imprisoned, and ended his career as vice commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qianyuan had impeached Liu Jin as a censor, suffered court beating and imprisonment, and ended his days as vice commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 廩舉嘉靖末進士，授行人。

translations.literal: Lin passed the jinshi examination at the end of the Jiajing reign and was appointed an Imperial Messenger.
translations.idiomatic: Lin passed the jinshi examination in the final years of the Jiajing reign and was appointed an Imperial Messenger.

sentences.zh: 隆慶三年擢御史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longqing, he was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 3 he was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 因地震，請加禮中宮。

translations.literal: Because of an earthquake, he requested increased ceremonial honors for the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Citing an earthquake, he memorialized that greater ceremonial honors be shown to the empress.

sentences.zh: 已，出核陜西四鎮兵食。

translations.literal: Afterward, he was sent out to audit the grain supplies of the four garrisons of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was then dispatched to audit grain supplies for Shaanxi's four frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 斥將吏隱占卒數萬人歸伍。

translations.literal: He denounced generals and officials who had secretly registered tens of thousands of soldiers and returned them to the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He exposed officers who had concealed tens of thousands of men on their registers and restored them to active service.

sentences.zh: 固原州海剌都之地，密邇松山，為楚府牧地。

translations.literal: The land of Hailadu in Guyuan Prefecture, close to Songshan, was pastureland of the Chu princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Pastureland belonging to the Chu princely establishment lay at Hailadu in Guyuan Prefecture, near Songshan.

sentences.zh: 廩言楚府封武昌，牧地在塞下，與寇接，王所收四五百金，而奸宄窟穴，弊甚大，宜諭使獻之朝廷。

translations.literal: Lin stated that the Chu establishment had been enfeoffed at Wuchang and its pastures were below the border, adjoining bandits; the prince collected four or five hundred taels of gold, yet scoundrels made their dens there—the harm was very great—and they ought to be instructed to surrender it to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Lin argued that although the Chu establishment had been enfeoffed at Wuchang, its pastures lay below the border hard against enemy territory; the prince drew only four or five hundred taels from them, yet outlaws used the land as a hideout, causing grave harm. He urged that the prince be ordered to turn the pastures over to the court.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 已，改巡茶馬。

translations.literal: Afterward, his post was changed to tea-and-horse circuit inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He was then reassigned as tea-and-horse circuit inspector.

sentences.zh: 七苑牧地，養馬八千七百餘匹，而占地五萬五千三百頃有奇。

translations.literal: The pastures of the seven stud farms raised more than eight thousand seven hundred horses but occupied more than fifty-three thousand three hundred qing of land.
translations.idiomatic: The seven stud farms pastured more than eight thousand seven hundred horses yet occupied over fifty-three thousand three hundred qing of land.

sentences.zh: 廩但給萬二千二百餘頃，歲益課二萬。

translations.literal: Lin allocated only a little more than twelve thousand two hundred qing and increased the annual levy by twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Lin certified only a little over twelve thousand two hundred qing and raised the annual tax by twenty thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 萬曆元年，巡按浙江。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli, he served as touring inspector of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 1 he toured Zhejiang as inspector.

sentences.zh: 請祀建文朝忠臣十二人，從祀王守仁於文廟。

translations.literal: He requested sacrifices to the twelve loyal ministers of the Jianwen reign and the associate worship of Wang Shouren in the Confucian temple.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned for sacrifices to twelve loyal ministers of the Jianwen reign and for Wang Shouren to be enshrined alongside them in the Confucian temple.

sentences.zh: 尋擢太僕少卿，再遷南京太僕卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, then again transferred to Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and later transferred to Nanjing as its minister.

sentences.zh: 九年，由光祿卿改右僉都御史，巡撫陜西。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, from Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments he was changed to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 9 he moved from Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 時方核天下隱田，大吏爭希張居正指增賦，廩令如額而止。

translations.literal: At that time hidden fields throughout the empire were being investigated; great officials all sought to follow Zhang Juzheng's intent to increase taxation, but Lin ordered that assessments stop at the fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: While a nationwide audit of concealed land was under way, senior officials competed to follow Zhang Juzheng's lead in raising taxes, but Lin insisted assessments go no beyond the established quota.

sentences.zh: 境內回回部常群行拾麥穗，間或草竊，耀州以變告。

translations.literal: Within the province Hui communities often went in groups to glean wheat spikes, occasionally committing petty theft; Yaozhou reported this as a disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Hui communities in the province often went out in groups to glean wheat, sometimes turning to petty theft, and Yaozhou reported trouble brewing.

sentences.zh: 廩撫諭之，戮數人，變遂定；

translations.literal: Lin soothed and instructed them, executed several men, and the disturbance was settled;
translations.idiomatic: Lin appeased them and put several ringleaders to death, and the unrest subsided;

sentences.zh: 令拾麥毋帶兵器，儕偶不得至十人。

translations.literal: he ordered that when gleaning wheat they were not to carry weapons and groups were not to exceed ten persons.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled that gleaners must go unarmed and in parties of no more than ten.

sentences.zh: 進右副都御史，移撫浙江。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief and transferred to grand coordinator of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief, he was reassigned as grand coordinator of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 先以賞貢使，歲增造彩幣二千。

translations.literal: Previously, to reward tribute envoys, two thousand additional ceremonial silks were manufactured annually.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang had earlier been required to weave two thousand extra bolts of ceremonial silk each year to reward tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 廩請均之福建及徽、寧諸府，從之。

translations.literal: Lin requested that the burden be shared among Fujian and the prefectures of Huizhou and Ningguo; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Lin asked that the obligation be apportioned among Fujian, Huizhou, Ningguo, and other prefectures, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 已，請減上供織造，不許。

translations.literal: Afterward, he requested a reduction in tribute weaving for the court; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He later petitioned to cut palace weaving quotas, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 遷工部右侍郎，召改刑部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Minister of Works and then summoned and changed to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Vice Minister of Works, then recalled and moved to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 進兵部左侍郎，以官卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Minister of War and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Vice Minister of War and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as a minister.

sentences.zh: 廩初從歐陽德、鄒守益遊。

translations.literal: In his early years Lin associated with Ouyang De and Zou Shouyi.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Lin studied under Ouyang De and Zou Shouyi.

sentences.zh: 制行醇謹，故所至有立。

translations.literal: His conduct was pure and careful, so wherever he went he achieved results.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and meticulous in his ways, he left a mark wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 賈三近，字德修，嶧縣人。

translations.literal: Jia Sanjin, style Dexiu, was a native of Yixian.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sanjin, styled Dexiu, came from Yixian.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the second year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Longqing 2.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，授吏科給事中。

translations.literal: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed a supervising secretary in the Department of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Chosen as a Hanlin bachelor, he was appointed supervising secretary in the Department of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 四年六月，疏言：「善治者守法以宜民，去其太甚而已。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year he memorialized: "Those who govern well uphold the law to suit the people, removing only what is excessive.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Longqing 4 he submitted a memorial: "Good government means holding to the law for the people's benefit and correcting nothing beyond what is truly excessive.

sentences.zh: 今廟堂之令不信於郡縣，郡縣之令不信於小民。

translations.literal: Today orders from the court are not trusted in the prefectures and counties, and orders from the prefectures and counties are not trusted by common people.
translations.idiomatic: Court orders no longer carry weight in the counties, and county orders no longer carry weight among the people.

sentences.zh: 蠲租矣而催科愈急，振濟矣而追逋自如，恤刑矣而冤死相望。

translations.literal: Rent has been remitted yet tax collection grows more urgent; relief has been granted yet pursuit of arrears continues as before; mercy in punishments has been proclaimed yet wrongful deaths stretch in sight of one another.
translations.idiomatic: Tax exemptions are declared, yet collection grows harsher; relief is ordered, yet officials chase arrears as before; mercy in judgment is proclaimed, yet the innocent still die in droves.

sentences.zh: 正額之輸，上供之需，邊疆之費，雖欲損毫厘不可得。

translations.literal: Regular quota payments, court supply needs, and frontier expenses—even if one wished to reduce a fraction, it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed tax quotas, palace requisitions, and frontier expenses cannot be trimmed by so much as a whisker.

sentences.zh: 形格勢制，莫可如何。

translations.literal: Form and circumstance restrain one; nothing can be done.
translations.idiomatic: Circumstance ties one's hands; there is no way forward.

sentences.zh: 且監司考課，多取振作集事之人，而輕寬平和易之士，守令雖賢，安養之心漸移於苛察，撫字之念日奪於征輸，民安得不困！

translations.literal: Moreover, in evaluating supervising officials, most take those who rouse themselves and gather affairs, while they slight men who are lenient, peaceful, and easygoing; even if magistrates are worthy, their hearts for nurturing the people gradually shift toward harsh scrutiny, and their thought of comforting the people is daily seized by levy and transport—how can the people not be distressed!
translations.idiomatic: Provincial inspectors rate officials mainly on bustle and visible results, not on calm and humane governance; even capable magistrates gradually trade care for the people for nit-picking scrutiny, and humane administration gives way to tax collection—how can the people not suffer?

sentences.zh: 乞戒有司務守法。

translations.literal: I beg that officials be admonished to hold firmly to the law.
translations.idiomatic: I urge that all officials be warned to keep faithfully to the law.

sentences.zh: 而監司殿最毋但取旦夕功，失惇大之體。

translations.literal: And in ranking supervising officials, do not take only morning-and-evening achievements and lose the great substance of generous governance.
translations.idiomatic: And when ranking provincial superiors, do not reward short-term bustle at the expense of steady, generous governance.

sentences.zh: 」已，復疏言：「撫按諸臣遇州縣長吏，率重甲科而輕鄉舉。

translations.literal: " Having done so, he again memorialized: "When grand coordinators and regional inspectors meet with prefectural and county magistrates, they generally favor jinshi graduates and slight those from the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: " He then submitted another memorial: "When grand coordinators and regional inspectors deal with prefectural and county magistrates, they invariably favor jinshi graduates and look down on provincial graduates.
