sentences.zh: 同一寬也，在進士則為撫字，在舉人則為姑息。

translations.literal: The same leniency in a jinshi is called nurturing the people; in a provincial graduate it is called indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: The same leniency in a jinshi is praised as humane governance; in a provincial graduate it is dismissed as lax indulgence.

sentences.zh: 同一嚴也，在進士則為精明，在舉人則為苛戾。

translations.literal: The same severity in a jinshi is called acuity; in a provincial graduate it is called harsh cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: The same severity in a jinshi is called shrewd administration; in a provincial graduate it is called cruel harshness.

sentences.zh: 是以為舉人者，非華顛豁齒不就選；

translations.literal: Therefore those who are provincial graduates do not accept selection unless their hair is white and teeth are missing;
translations.idiomatic: Provincial graduates refuse appointment until they are gray-haired and worn with age;

sentences.zh: 人或裹足毀裳，息心仕進。

translations.literal: some people wrap their feet and ruin their robes, calming their hearts and ceasing to pursue office.
translations.idiomatic: some lose heart altogether and withdraw from public life.

sentences.zh: 夫鄉舉豈乏才良，宜令勉就是途，因行激勸。

translations.literal: Are there not talented and good men among provincial graduates? They ought to be urged to enter this path and encouraged as they go.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial examination produces able men; they should be urged to serve and actively encouraged on their way.

sentences.zh: 」詔皆俞允。

translations.literal: " The edict approved all.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne approved both petitions.

sentences.zh: 再遷左給事中，勘事貴州。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Left Supervising Secretary and assigned to investigate affairs in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Supervising Secretary and sent to investigate a case in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 中道罷遣，遂請急歸。

translations.literal: Midway he was dismissed and sent back; he then requested emergency leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The mission was cancelled en route and he was sent home; he then took emergency leave.

sentences.zh: 神宗嗣位，起戶科給事中。

translations.literal: When the Shenzong Emperor succeeded to the throne, he was recalled as supervising secretary in the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong ascended the throne, he was recalled as supervising secretary in the Department of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 萬曆元年，平江伯陳王謨以太后家姻，夤緣得鎮湖廣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wanli, the Duke of Pingjiang Chen Wangmo, through kinship with the empress dowager's family, sought by connections to obtain command of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 1 the Duke of Pingjiang, Chen Wangmo, used ties to the empress dowager's clan to seek command of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 三近劾其垢穢，乃不遣。

translations.literal: Sanjin impeached him for filth and corruption, and he was not sent.
translations.idiomatic: Sanjin impeached him for corruption and debauchery, and the appointment was blocked.

sentences.zh: 給事中雒遵、御史景嵩、韓必顯劾譚綸被謫，三近率同列救之，詔增供用庫黃蠟歲二萬五千，三近等又諫，皆不從。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries Luo Zun, the censors Jing Song and Han Bixian impeached Tan Lun and were punished; Sanjin led his colleagues to rescue them. An edict increased the annual yellow wax for the supply depot by twenty-five thousand; Sanjin and the others again remonstrated—all were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: After supervising secretary Luo Zun and censors Jing Song and Han Bixian impeached Tan Lun and were punished, Sanjin led his colleagues in their defense. When the court ordered twenty-five thousand more units of yellow wax for the supply depot, Sanjin and his colleagues remonstrated again—all to no avail.

sentences.zh: 時方行海運，多覆舟，以三近言罷其役。

translations.literal: At that time sea transport was being implemented; many boats capsized, and because of Sanjin's words that service was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Sea transport had just been introduced, but so many ships sank that, on Sanjin's advice, the scheme was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 肅王縉貴，隆慶間用賄以輔國將軍襲封，至是又請復莊田，三近再疏爭，遂弗予。

translations.literal: Prince Su, an honored noble, had in the Longqing period used bribes to inherit as Assistant State General; now he again requested restoration of his estate lands—Sanjin twice memorialized in opposition, and it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Su, a man of great influence, had bought his way to the title of Assistant State General under Longqing; he now petitioned to recover his estate lands, but Sanjin protested twice and the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 初，有令征賦以八分為率，不及者議罰。

translations.literal: At first there was an order that tax collection use eighty percent as the rate, and failure to reach it was to be punished by deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: At first the court set eighty percent collection as the benchmark and threatened penalties for shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 三近請地雕敝者減一分，詔從之。

translations.literal: Sanjin requested that for lands that were carved up and exhausted one percent be reduced; an edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Sanjin asked that devastated regions be allowed one percent below the quota, and the throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 中官溫泰請盡輸關稅、鹽課於內庫，三近言課稅本餉邊，今屯田半蕪，開中法壞，塞下所資惟此，茍歸內帑，必誤邊計。

translations.literal: The eunuch Wen Tai requested that all customs duties and salt taxes be paid entirely into the inner treasury; Sanjin said that tax revenues originally provisioned the frontier—now half the military colonies are overgrown and the frontier exchange system is broken; what the border relies on is only this; if it goes to the inner treasury, the border plan will surely be mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuch Wen Tai proposed routing all customs and salt revenue into the inner treasury, Sanjin warned that those funds fed the frontier; with military colonies half abandoned and the salt-for-grain exchange system in ruins, the border depended on this income alone—diverting it to the private purse would wreck frontier finance.

sentences.zh: 議乃寢。

translations.literal: The proposal was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 頃之，擢太常少卿。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 再遷南京光祿卿，請假歸。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments at Nanjing and requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to Nanjing as Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and went home on leave.

sentences.zh: 十二年，召掌光祿，其秋，拜右僉都御史，巡撫保定。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was summoned to head the Court of Imperial Entertainments; that autumn he was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 12 he was recalled to head the Court of Imperial Entertainments; that autumn he was made Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Baoding.

sentences.zh: 畿輔大饑，振貸有方。

translations.literal: The capital region suffered great famine; he had effective methods for relief and loans.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck the capital region, he organized relief and grain loans with skill.

sentences.zh: 召拜大理卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 未上，以親老歸養。

translations.literal: Before taking up the post, because his parents were elderly he returned home to support them.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take office, he returned home to care for his aged parents.

sentences.zh: 起兵部右侍郎，復以親老辭，不許。

translations.literal: He was raised to Right Vice Minister of War, but again pleaded elderly parents and was not permitted to decline.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Right Vice Minister of War, he again pleaded the need to care for his parents, but the court refused to let him resign.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 李頤，字惟貞，余幹人。

translations.literal: Li Yi, style Weizhen, was a native of Yugan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi, styled Weizhen, came from Yugan.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the second year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Longqing 2.

sentences.zh: 授中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed a Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 博習典故，負才名。

translations.literal: He was broadly versed in precedents and bore a reputation for talent.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply versed in institutional precedent, he earned a reputation for literary talent.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，擢御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli, he was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign he was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 同官胡涍、景嵩、韓必顯，給事中雒遵相繼獲譴，抗疏申救，不聽。

translations.literal: His colleagues Hu Gan, Jing Song, and Han Bixian, and the supervising secretary Luo Zun were in succession punished; he submitted a bold memorial to plead for them, but the court did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When his colleagues Hu Gan, Jing Song, and Han Bixian and supervising secretary Luo Zun were punished in turn, he memorialized boldly in their defense, but the throne paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 清軍湖廣、廣西，請免士民遠戍，只充傍近衛所軍，制可。

translations.literal: Inspecting troops in Huguang and Guangxi, he requested exemption for gentry and commoners from distant garrison service, allowing them to serve only in nearby guard units; an imperial decree approved.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting troops in Huguang and Guangxi, he petitioned to spare local gentry and commoners from distant frontier garrison duty and let them serve only in nearby guard units; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 忤張居正，出為湖州知府。

translations.literal: He offended Zhang Juzheng and was sent out as prefect of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing Zhang Juzheng, he was demoted to prefect of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷蘇松兵備副使、湖廣按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner for military preparedness in Su-Song and surveillance commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Su-Song vice commissioner for military preparedness and then to Huguang surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鄖陽兵變，知府沈鈇且得罪，頤為白其冤，而密殲首亂者。

translations.literal: When troops mutinied at Yunyang, the prefect Shen Yue was about to be punished; Yi cleared his innocence and secretly wiped out the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yunyang mutiny, when Prefect Shen Yue faced punishment, Yi vindicated him while quietly eliminating the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 以母喪歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 起故官，蒞陜西，進河南右布政使。

translations.literal: Recalled to his former office, he arrived in Shaanxi and was promoted to Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to office, he served in Shaanxi before advancing to Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 擢右僉都御史，巡撫順天。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 進右副都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 以定亂兵進兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: For quelling the mutinous troops he was advanced to Right Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: For suppressing the mutiny he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 長昂桀驁，頤與總兵王保擒其心腹小郎兒等七人，賊遂軿。

translations.literal: Chang Ang was arrogant; Yi and the regional commander Wang Bao captured his trusted followers Xiao Lang'er and six others, and the bandits then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mongol leader Chang Ang grew defiant, Yi and Regional Commander Wang Bao seized his lieutenant Xiao Lang'er and six others, and the rebels submitted.

sentences.zh: 已，別部伯牙入寇，督將士敗之羅文峪，進左侍郎。

translations.literal: Afterward, another band under Boya invaded; he supervised officers and men and defeated them at Luowen Pass, and was promoted to Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: When a separate band under Boya raided the border, he led the troops to victory at Luowen Pass and was promoted to Left Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 久之，進右都御史。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時礦稅使四出。

translations.literal: At that time mining-tax envoys were dispatched in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Mining-tax commissioners were then being sent out across the empire.

sentences.zh: 馬堂駐天津，王忠駐昌平，王虎駐保定，張曄駐通州。

translations.literal: Ma Tang was stationed at Tianjin, Wang Zhong at Changping, Wang Hu at Baoding, and Zhang Ye at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Tang held Tianjin, Wang Zhong Changping, Wang Hu Baoding, and Zhang Ye Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 頤疏言：「燕京王氣所鐘，去陵寢近，開鑿必損靈氣。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized: "Yanjing is where royal qi converges; it is close to the imperial tombs—opening mines will surely damage spiritual power.
translations.idiomatic: Yi wrote: "The capital region concentrates the dynasty's vital energy and lies close to the imperial tombs—mining there would violate sacred ground.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「畿輔地荒歲儉，而敕使誅求，不遺纖屑，恐臨清激變之慘，復見輦轂下。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The capital region's land is barren and the year is lean, yet imperial envoys squeeze without leaving the slightest scrap—I fear the horrors of the Linqing uprising will again appear beneath the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: " He added: "The capital districts are barren and harvests poor, yet imperial agents squeeze every penny—I fear a disaster like the Linqing riot will erupt again at the emperor's doorstep.

sentences.zh: 」已，遼東稅使高淮誣劾山海同知羅大器，頤復言：「內監外僚，初無統攝，且遼陽礦稅，何預薊門？

translations.literal: " Afterward, the Liaodong tax envoy Gao Huai falsely impeached Vice Prefect Luo Daqi of Shanhai; Yi again said: "Inner-court eunuchs and outer-court officials have from the first had no command relationship, and what has Liaoyang mining-tax to do with the Jizhou Pass?
translations.idiomatic: " Later, when Liaodong mining-tax commissioner Gao Huai falsely impeached Shanhai Vice Prefect Luo Daqi, Yi protested again: "Palace eunuchs hold no authority over civil officials, and what business has a Liaodong mining tax in the Jizhou garrison?

sentences.zh: 若皆效淮所為，有司將無遺類。

translations.literal: If all follow what Huai has done, local officials will have no survivors.
translations.idiomatic: If every agent followed Huai's example, no official would be left standing.

sentences.zh: 陛下奉天之權，制馭宇內，今盡落宦豎手，朝奏夕報，如響應聲。

translations.literal: Your Majesty holds Heaven's authority and commands all within the realm; today it has entirely fallen into the hands of eunuch attendants—memorials submitted in the morning receive replies by evening, like an echo answering a sound.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty alone holds Heaven's mandate over the realm, yet power has passed entirely into eunuchs' hands—memorials filed in the morning receive verdicts by evening, as if by reflex.

sentences.zh: 縱所劾當罪，尚非所以為名，何況無辜，暴加摧折。

translations.literal: Even if those impeached were guilty, this would still not be the way to make a name; how much less when the innocent are violently crushed.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the accused deserved punishment, this would still be no way to govern; how much worse when innocent men are crushed without cause.

sentences.zh: 」皆不報。

translations.literal: " None received response.
translations.idiomatic: " None of his protests drew any reply.

sentences.zh: 頤在鎮十年，威望大著。

translations.literal: Yi was at his post for ten years; his prestige was greatly displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Yi held his post for ten years, and his authority grew formidable.

sentences.zh: 中使憚頤廉正，畿民少安。

translations.literal: Inner-court envoys feared Yi's integrity and uprightness, and the people of the capital region were somewhat at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Palace envoys feared his integrity, and the people of the capital region knew a measure of relief.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以工部右侍郎代劉東星管理河道。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was made Right Vice Minister of Works in place of Liu Dongxing to manage the waterways.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 29 he succeeded Liu Dongxing as Right Vice Minister of Works with charge of the canal works.

sentences.zh: 議上築決口，下疏故道，為經久計。

translations.literal: He proposed building up the breached dike above and dredging the old channel below, as a long-term plan.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed reinforcing the breach above and clearing the old channel below as a lasting remedy.

sentences.zh: 甫兩月，以勞卒。

translations.literal: Only two months had passed when he died from exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: After barely two months he died from overwork.

sentences.zh: 贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 頤仕宦三十餘年，敝車羸馬，布衣蔬食。

translations.literal: Yi served in office for more than thirty years with a worn cart, emaciated horses, plain clothes, and simple food.
translations.idiomatic: Over more than thirty years in office he traveled in a broken cart with thin horses and lived on plain clothes and simple fare.

sentences.zh: 初為御史，首請祀胡居仁於文廟，寢未行。

translations.literal: When he first became a censor, he was the first to request worship of Hu Juren in the Confucian temple; the proposal was shelved and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: As a new censor he had been the first to petition for Hu Juren's enshrinement in the Confucian temple, but the request never took effect.

sentences.zh: 見居仁裔孫希祖幼且貧，字以女，養之於家。

translations.literal: Seeing that Juren's descendant Xizu was young and poor, he betrothed his daughter to him and raised him in his household.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Hu Juren's great-grandson Xizu was still a boy and in poverty, he gave him his daughter in marriage and brought him up in his own home.

sentences.zh: 弟謙早卒，以己蔭畀其子。

translations.literal: His younger brother Qian died early; he transferred his own hereditary privilege to Qian's son.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Qian had died young, so he surrendered his own inherited privilege to Qian's son.

sentences.zh: 朱鴻謨，字文甫，益都人。

translations.literal: Zhu Hongmo, styled Wenfu, was a native of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hongmo, courtesy name Wenfu, came from Yidu.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fifth year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fifth year of the Longqing reign.

sentences.zh: 授吉安推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating magistrate at Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 識鄒元標於諸生，厚禮之。

translations.literal: He recognized Zou Yuanbiao among the students and treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Among the local students he recognized Zou Yuanbiao and honored him with exceptional respect.

sentences.zh: 擢南京御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 元標及吳中行等得罪，鴻謨疏救，語侵居正，斥為民。

translations.literal: When Yuanbiao, Wu Zhongxing, and others were punished, Hongmo memorialized to save them; his language impugned Juzheng, and he was dismissed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: After Zou Yuanbiao, Wu Zhongxing, and others fell afoul of the court, Hongmo submitted a memorial in their defense; because his words impugned Zhang Juzheng, he was stripped of office and sent home as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 鴻謨歸，杜門講學，不入城市。

translations.literal: Hongmo returned home, closed his doors to lecture on learning, and did not enter the cities.
translations.idiomatic: Back home, Hongmo shut his gates to teach and refused to set foot in the towns.

sentences.zh: 居正卒，起故官，出按江西。

translations.literal: When Juzheng died, he was restored to his former office and sent out to inspect Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Juzheng's death he was recalled to his former rank and dispatched to conduct an inspection tour of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 奏蠲水災賦，請減饒州磁器，不報。

translations.literal: He memorialized to remit taxes after flood damage and requested a reduction in Raozhou porcelain tribute; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned for tax relief after the floods and asked that Raozhou's porcelain levy be cut, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 又疏薦建言削籍者，忤旨，奪俸。

translations.literal: He again memorialized recommending men who had been struck from the rolls for remonstrance; he offended the imperial will and had his salary suspended.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended officials who had been expelled from the rolls for speaking out, and for defying the throne his stipend was withheld.

sentences.zh: 擢光祿少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 由大理少卿擢右僉都御史，提督操江。

translations.literal: From Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and put in charge of the Yangtze patrol.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, he was made Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief with command over the Yangtze patrol fleet.

sentences.zh: 改撫應天、蘇州十府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as grand coordinator of the ten prefectures of Yingtian and Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as grand coordinator over the ten prefectures of Yingtian and Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 引二祖節儉之德，請裁上供織造，報聞。

translations.literal: Citing the frugal virtue of the two founding emperors, he requested cuts in palace textile manufacture; the court acknowledged the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Invoking the thrift of the dynasty's two founders, he asked that imperial textile orders be reduced, and the court noted his request.

sentences.zh: 吳中徭役不均，令一以田為準，不及百畝者無役，縣為立籍，定等差。

translations.literal: Corvée labor in Wu was unevenly distributed; he ordered that land alone be the standard, that holders of less than one hundred mu owe no service, and that counties keep registers and fix gradations.
translations.idiomatic: Because corvée burdens in the Wu region fell unevenly, he made landholding the sole measure: anyone with less than one hundred mu owed no labor duty, and each county was to keep a register and set graded obligations.

sentences.zh: 貴遊子弟恣里中，無賴者與共為非，遠近訛言謂有不軌謀。

translations.literal: Young scions of noble families ran wild in the villages; ruffians joined them in wrongdoing, and rumors near and far said there was a seditious plot.
translations.idiomatic: Well-born youths ran riot through the countryside, local thugs joined their misdeeds, and wild talk spread that a treasonous conspiracy was afoot.

sentences.zh: 鴻謨盡捕之，上疏告變。

translations.literal: Hongmo arrested them all and memorialized to report an emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Hongmo seized them all and memorialized the throne with an alarm of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 朝議將用兵，兵部主事伍袁萃亟言於尚書石星，令覆勘，乃解。

translations.literal: Court discussion turned toward sending troops; the Ministry of War section chief Wu Yuancui urgently spoke to Minister Shi Xing, ordering a reinvestigation, and the matter was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: The court was on the verge of mobilizing troops when Wu Yuancui, a section chief in the Ministry of War, urgently urged Minister Shi Xing to order a fresh inquiry; only then was the crisis defused.

sentences.zh: 鴻謨尋入為刑部右侍郎，卒官。

translations.literal: Hongmo soon entered the capital as Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Justice and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Hongmo was soon recalled to serve as Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Justice, and he died in that post.

sentences.zh: 不能斂，僚屬醵金以辦。

translations.literal: He had no means for burial; his colleagues pooled money to arrange it.
translations.idiomatic: His family could not afford a proper burial, so his colleagues pooled funds to see to it.

sentences.zh: 贈刑部尚書，謚恭介。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Minister of Justice and given the posthumous name Gongjie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Justice with the posthumous title Gongjie, "Respectful and Upright."

sentences.zh: 蕭彥，字思學，涇縣人。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan, styled Sixue, was a native of Jing County.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan, courtesy name Sixue, came from Jing County.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fifth year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fifth year of the Longqing reign.

sentences.zh: 除杭州推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating magistrate at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三年，擢兵科給事中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wanli he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Wanli reign he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of War.

sentences.zh: 自塞上多警，邊吏輒假招降幸賞。

translations.literal: Since the frontier was often alarmed, border officials repeatedly used feigned surrender to seek rewards.
translations.idiomatic: With alarms multiplying on the northern frontier, border officials kept staging sham surrenders in hopes of bounty.

sentences.zh: 彥言：「議招逆黨，為中國逋亡設耳，乃欲以此招漠北敵人。

translations.literal: Yan said: "The policy of recruiting rebel factions was devised only for fugitives within China, yet now they wish to use it to recruit enemies from beyond the northern deserts.
translations.idiomatic: Yan argued: "The policy of accepting surrenders from rebel bands was meant for fugitives within the empire, not for trying to win over enemies from beyond the northern steppe.

sentences.zh: 夫李俊、滿四等休養百年，稱亂一旦，降人不可處內地明矣。

translations.literal: Men such as Li Jun and Man Si rested and recovered for a hundred years, then in a single day were called rebels; that surrendered people must not be settled in the interior is already clear.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jun, Man Si, and their like had been allowed to recover for a century, then rose in rebellion overnight—the lesson that surrendered peoples must not be settled in the interior is plain enough.

sentences.zh: 宜一切報罷。

translations.literal: All such proposals should be rejected outright.
translations.idiomatic: Every such proposal ought to be rejected outright.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 以工科左給事中閱視陜西四鎮邊務。

translations.literal: As Left Supervising Secretary in the Bureau of Works he inspected border affairs of the four garrisons of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: As Left Supervising Secretary in the Bureau of Works he toured the border defenses of Shaanxi's four garrisons.

sentences.zh: 還奏訓兵、儲餉十事，並允行。

translations.literal: On his return he memorialized ten measures for drilling troops and storing provisions; all were approved and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he submitted ten recommendations on troop training and grain reserves, all of which were approved.

sentences.zh: 尋進戶科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary in the Bureau of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary in the Bureau of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 初，行丈量法，延、寧二鎮益田萬八千餘頃。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the land-survey method was applied, the two garrisons of Yan and Ning gained more than eighteen thousand additional qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: When land surveys were first carried out, the Yan and Ning garrisons had gained more than eighteen thousand qing of newly registered fields.

sentences.zh: 總督高文薦請三年征賦，彥言：「西北墾荒永免科稅，祖制也。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Gao Wenjian requested levying taxes after three years; Yan said: "In the northwest, newly reclaimed land is permanently exempt from taxation—this is ancestral institution.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Gao Wenjian asked that taxes be collected after three years on the new land; Yan replied: "Permanent tax exemption for reclaimed land in the northwest is ancestral law.

sentences.zh: 況二鎮多沙磧，奈何定永額，使初集流庸懷去誌。

translations.literal: Moreover the two garrisons are mostly sandy waste—how can a permanent quota be fixed and make newly gathered vagrants harbor thoughts of leaving?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, much of the land in those two garrisons is sandy waste—why fix a permanent quota and drive newly settled refugees to think of leaving again?

sentences.zh: 」遂除前令。

translations.literal: " The earlier order was thereupon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: " The earlier order was accordingly revoked.

sentences.zh: 詔購金珠，已，停市，而命以其直輸內庫。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the purchase of gold and pearls; afterward the market was halted, but the command was given to deliver their value into the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had ordered the purchase of gold and pearls; when the buying was stopped, the court still commanded that the equivalent value be paid into the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 彥言不當虛外府以實內藏，不聽。

translations.literal: Yan said one must not empty the outer treasuries to fill the inner storehouse; the court did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yan argued that provincial coffers should not be drained to swell the imperial vault, but his protest went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 尋上言：「察吏之道，不宜視催科為殿最。

translations.literal: Soon he submitted: "In the way of inspecting officials, one should not take tax collection as the sole measure of merit.
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized: "In evaluating officials, tax collection alone should not decide their standing.

sentences.zh: 昨隆慶五年詔征賦不及八分者，停有司俸。

translations.literal: Previously, in the fifth year of Longqing, an edict said that where tax collection did not reach eight-tenths, the salaries of local officials would be suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Longqing an edict had ruled that officials who collected less than eighty percent of the levy would forfeit their salaries.

sentences.zh: 至萬曆四年則又以九分為及格，仍令帶征宿負二分，是民歲輸十分以上也。

translations.literal: By the fourth year of Wanli nine-tenths became the passing mark, while officials were still ordered to collect an additional two-tenths of old arrears—thus the people paid more than ten-tenths each year.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth year of Wanli the passing mark had been raised to ninety percent, yet officials were still required to collect an extra twenty percent of old arrears—so the people were paying more than the full levy every year.

sentences.zh: 有司憚考成，必重以敲撲。

translations.literal: Local officials, fearing performance review, inevitably intensified beatings and floggings.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified of failing their assessments, local officials inevitably resorted to heavier beatings.

sentences.zh: 民力不勝，則流亡隨之。

translations.literal: When the people's strength could not bear it, flight followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the people could no longer endure the burden, flight followed.

sentences.zh: 臣以為九分與帶征二議，不宜並行。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that the two policies—the nine-tenths standard and the additional collection of arrears—should not be carried out together.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the ninety-percent standard and the extra arrears collection should not be enforced at the same time.

sentences.zh: 所謂寬一分，民受一分之賜也。

translations.literal: What is called easing by one part is a gift the people receive in one part.
translations.idiomatic: Every fraction of relief the court grants is a fraction of mercy the people actually receive.

sentences.zh: 」部議允行。

translations.literal: " The ministry deliberated and approved implementation.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministry deliberated and approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 未幾，浙江巡撫張佳胤復以舊例請，部又從之。

translations.literal: Before long, Zhejiang Grand Coordinator Zhang Jiayin again requested the old practice, and the ministry again followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Zhejiang grand coordinator Zhang Jiayin petitioned to restore the old practice, and the ministry again agreed.

sentences.zh: 彥疏爭，乃詔如新令。

translations.literal: Yan memorialized in protest, and only then was an edict issued according to the new rule.
translations.idiomatic: Yan protested in a memorial, and the throne finally ordered that the new rule stand.

sentences.zh: 詔取黃金三千二百兩，彥請納戶部言減其半，不從。

translations.literal: An edict demanded three thousand two hundred taels of gold; Yan requested, following the Ministry of Revenue's advice, that the amount be halved; the court did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict called for thirty-two hundred taels of gold, Yan asked—on the Ministry of Revenue's advice—that the levy be cut in half, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 擢太常少卿，以右僉都御史巡撫貴州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and, as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, served as grand coordinator of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 都勻答千巖苗叛，土官蒙詔不能制，彥檄副使楊寅秋破擒之。

translations.literal: The Miao of Duyun and Daqianyan rebelled; the native official Meng Zhao could not control them; Yan dispatched Vice Commissioner Yang Yinqiu, who broke them and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Miao of Duyun and Daqianyan rose in rebellion and the native official Meng Zhao could not suppress them, Yan sent Vice Commissioner Yang Yinqiu, who routed the rebels and took them captive.

sentences.zh: 宣慰安國亨詭言獻大木，被賚。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner An Guoheng falsely claimed to offer great timber and received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner An Guoheng falsely claimed he was presenting great timber and was rewarded for it.

sentences.zh: 及征木無有，為彥所劾。

translations.literal: When timber was requisitioned and none was found, he was impeached by Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When the timber was demanded and none appeared, Yan impeached him.

sentences.zh: 國亨懼，誣商奪其木，訐彥於朝。

translations.literal: Guoheng, in fear, falsely accused merchants of seizing his timber and denounced Yan at court.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing punishment, Guoheng falsely accused merchants of stealing his timber and denounced Yan at court.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，欲罪彥。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and wished to punish Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and intended to punish Yan.

sentences.zh: 大學士申時行等言國亨反噬，輕朝廷，帝乃止。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Shen Shixing and others said Guoheng had turned to bite back and slighted the court; the emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Shen Shixing and others argued that Guoheng had turned on his accuser and treated the court with contempt, and the emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 改撫雲南。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as grand coordinator of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as grand coordinator of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 時用師隴川，副將鄧子龍不善御軍，兵大噪，守備姜忻撫定之。

translations.literal: At the time troops were being used in Longchuan; Vice General Deng Zilong was poor at controlling the army, the soldiers raised a great clamor, and Garrison Commander Jiang Xin pacified and settled them.
translations.idiomatic: While troops were engaged in Longchuan, Vice General Deng Zilong proved unable to command his men; the soldiers mutinied loudly, and Garrison Commander Jiang Xin restored order.

sentences.zh: 而其兵素驕，給餉少緩，遂作亂。

translations.literal: Yet those troops had long been arrogant; when rations were slightly delayed, they then rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: But those troops had long been unruly, and when pay was even slightly delayed they rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 鼓行至永昌，趨大理，抵瀾滄，過會城。

translations.literal: Beating drums they marched to Yongchang, pressed toward Dali, reached Lancang, and passed Huicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Beating drums as they marched, they advanced through Yongchang toward Dali, reached the Lancang River, and passed Huicheng.

sentences.zh: 彥調土、漢兵夾攻之，斬首八十，脅從皆撫散。

translations.literal: Yan mobilized native and Han troops to attack them from both sides, beheaded eighty, and pacified and dispersed all who had been coerced to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sent native and Han troops to attack them from both flanks, killed eighty ringleaders, and pacified and dispersed those who had been forced to join.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賚銀幣。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, silver and silks were bestowed as reward.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was rewarded with silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 自緬甸叛，孟養、車裏二宣慰久不貢。

translations.literal: Since Burma rebelled, the two pacification commissioners of Mengyang and Cheli had long ceased tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the Burmese rebellion, the pacification commissioners of Mengyang and Cheli had long ceased sending tribute.

sentences.zh: 至是修貢，彥撫納之。

translations.literal: At this time they restored tribute; Yan received and accepted them with reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: When they now resumed tribute, Yan received them graciously.

sentences.zh: 尋以副都御史撫治鄖陽。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief to pacify and administer Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Vice Censor-in-Chief with charge over the Yunyang pacification district.

sentences.zh: 進兵部右侍郎，總制兩廣軍務。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of War and given overall command of military affairs in the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of War with overall command of military affairs in Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 日本躪朝鮮。

translations.literal: Japan trampled Korea.
translations.idiomatic: Japan invaded and overran Korea.

sentences.zh: 會暹羅入貢，其使請勤王，尚書石星因令發兵搗日本。

translations.literal: It happened that Siam came to offer tribute; its envoy requested to aid the royal house, and Minister Shi Xing therefore ordered troops sent to strike Japan.
translations.idiomatic: When Siam sent tribute, its envoy offered to march to the aid of the Ming throne, and Minister Shi Xing ordered troops dispatched to strike at Japan.

sentences.zh: 彥言暹羅處極西，去日本萬里，安能飛越大海，請罷其議。

translations.literal: Yan said Siam lies at the far west, ten thousand li from Japan—how could it fly across the great sea? He requested that the plan be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yan argued that Siam lay at the far western edge of the world, ten thousand li from Japan—no army could fly across such a sea—and asked that the scheme be dropped.

sentences.zh: 星執不從。

translations.literal: Xing stubbornly refused to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xing stubbornly refused.

sentences.zh: 既而暹羅兵卒不出。

translations.literal: Before long the Siamese troops ultimately did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: In the end no Siamese troops ever appeared.

sentences.zh: 召拜戶部右侍郎，尋卒。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Revenue; soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of the Right in the Ministry of Revenue, but died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 彥從同縣查鐸學，有誌行。

translations.literal: Yan studied under Zha Duo of the same county and had resolve and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had studied under his fellow townsman Zha Duo and was a man of firm purpose and integrity.

sentences.zh: 服官明習天下事，所在見稱。

translations.literal: In office he clearly understood affairs under Heaven and was praised wherever he served.
translations.idiomatic: In office he had a clear grasp of public affairs and won praise wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 後贈右都御史，謚定肅。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously granted Right Censor-in-Chief and given the posthumous name Dingsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously honored as Right Censor-in-Chief with the posthumous title Dingsu, "Steadfast and Solemn."

sentences.zh: 弟雍，廣東按察使。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yong was Surveillance Commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yong served as Surveillance Commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 宦績亞於彥，而學過之。

translations.literal: His official achievements were second to Yan's, but his learning surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: His record in office fell short of Yan's, but his scholarship surpassed his brother's.

sentences.zh: 時稱「二蕭」。

translations.literal: They were called at the time "the Two Xiaos."
translations.idiomatic: People of the day called them "the Two Xiaos."

sentences.zh: 查鐸，字子警，嘉靖四十五年進士。

translations.literal: Zha Duo, styled Zijing, became a jinshi in the forty-fifth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: Zha Duo, courtesy name Zijing, passed the metropolitan examination in the forty-fifth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 隆慶時，為刑科左給事中。

translations.literal: In the Longqing period he served as Left Supervising Secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longqing reign he served as Left Supervising Secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 忤大學士高拱，出為山西參議。

translations.literal: He offended Grand Secretary Gao Gong and was sent out as Administrative Commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After offending Grand Secretary Gao Gong, he was transferred out to serve as Administrative Commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初，官廣西副使，移疾歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli he served as Vice Commissioner of Guangxi, then cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign he served as Vice Commissioner in Guangxi, then resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 繕水西書院，講王畿、錢德洪之學，後進多歸之。

translations.literal: He repaired the Shuixi Academy, lectured on the learning of Wang Ji and Qian Dehong, and many younger scholars came to him.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the Shuixi Academy, taught the philosophy of Wang Ji and Qian Dehong, and drew many younger scholars to his school.

sentences.zh: 孫維城，字宗甫，丘縣人。

translations.literal: Sun Weicheng, styled Zongfu, was a native of Qiu County.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Weicheng, courtesy name Zongfu, came from Qiu County.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fifth year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fifth year of the Longqing reign.

sentences.zh: 歷知浚、太康、任丘三縣。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of the three counties of Jun, Taikang, and Renqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as magistrate of Jun, Taikang, and Renqiu.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十年，擢南京御史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Wanli he was promoted to censor at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Wanli reign he was promoted to censor in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 初，張居正不奔喪，寧國諸生吳仕期欲上書諫。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Juzheng did not leave office for mourning; the Ningguo student Wu Shiji wished to submit a memorial in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhang Juzheng refused to leave office to mourn his father, the Ningguo student Wu Shiji prepared a memorial of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 未發，太平同知龍宗武告之操江胡槚，以聞於居正。

translations.literal: Before it was sent, Taiping Vice Prefect Long Zongwu reported it to the Yangtze patrol commander Hu Zhen, who informed Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Before it could be sent, Taiping Vice Prefect Long Zongwu informed the Yangtze patrol commander Hu Zhen, who reported the matter to Zhang Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 會有偽為海瑞劾居正疏者，播之邸抄。

translations.literal: It happened that someone forged a memorial by Hai Rui impeaching Juzheng and circulated it in the capital gazette.
translations.idiomatic: About that time a forged memorial purporting to be Hai Rui's impeachment of Zhang Juzheng appeared in the capital gazette.

sentences.zh: 宗武意仕期，遂置獄，榜掠七日而卒。

translations.literal: Zongwu suspected Shiji, put him in prison, flogged him for seven days, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Long Zongwu assumed Shiji was responsible, threw him into prison, and had him beaten for seven days until he died.

sentences.zh: 居正死，仕期妻訟冤，維城疏言狀。

translations.literal: When Juzheng died, Shiji's wife sued over the injustice; Weicheng memorialized stating the facts.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Juzheng's death, Shiji's widow petitioned for redress, and Weicheng memorialized setting out the facts of the case.

sentences.zh: 槚已擢刑部侍郎，宗武湖廣參議，皆落職戍邊，天下快之。

translations.literal: Hu had already been promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Justice and Zongwu to Administrative Commissioner of Huguang; both were stripped of office and sent to frontier garrison duty, and all under Heaven rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhen had already risen to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Justice and Long Zongwu to Administrative Commissioner of Huguang; both were dismissed and banished to frontier service, to the satisfaction of the empire.

sentences.zh: 中官田玉提督太和山，請兼行分守事，帝許之，維城援祖制力陳不可。

translations.literal: The eunuch Tian Yu, supervising commissioner of Mount Taihe, requested also to perform separate garrison duties; the emperor approved, but Weicheng cited ancestral institution and forcefully stated it was impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Tian Yu, as commissioner of Mount Taihe, asked to assume separate garrison duties as well, the emperor agreed; Weicheng cited ancestral precedent and argued strenuously that this must not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 俄以救言官範俊，奪俸一年。

translations.literal: Soon, for interceding on behalf of the remonstrating official Fan Jun, his salary was suspended for one year.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, for defending the remonstrating official Fan Jun, he had his salary withheld for a year.

sentences.zh: 忤座主大學士許國，出為永平知府。

translations.literal: He offended his patron Grand Secretary Xu Guo and was sent out as prefect of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: After offending his patron Grand Secretary Xu Guo, he was transferred out to serve as prefect of Yongping.

sentences.zh: 遷赤城兵備副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner for military defense at Chicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Commissioner for defense at Chicheng.

sentences.zh: 繕亭障二百六十所，招史、車二部千餘人。

translations.literal: He repaired two hundred sixty lookout pavilions and barriers, and recruited more than a thousand men from the Shi and Che tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He restored two hundred sixty lookout posts and fortifications and enlisted over a thousand men from the Shi and Che tribes.

sentences.zh: 以功屢進按察使，兵備如故。

translations.literal: On account of merit he was repeatedly promoted to Surveillance Commissioner, while his military defense duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: For his accomplishments he was repeatedly promoted to Surveillance Commissioner, retaining his military defense commission.

sentences.zh: 部長安兔挾五千騎邀賞，維城請於督、撫，革其市賞而責之，戢不敢肆。

translations.literal: The tribal chief An Tu, bringing five thousand horsemen, came to demand rewards; Weicheng petitioned the governor-general and grand coordinator to abolish their border-market stipends and hold them accountable, whereupon they restrained themselves and dared not run riot.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribal chief An Tu arrived with five thousand horsemen to demand rewards, Weicheng appealed to the governor-general and grand coordinator to cancel their border-market stipends and hold them accountable; chastened, they no longer dared act with impunity.

sentences.zh: 尋以右布政使移守宣府，改廣東左布政使。

translations.literal: Soon, as Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, he was transferred to defend Xuanfu, then reassigned as Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred from his post as Right Provincial Administration Commissioner at Xuanfu to serve as Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，拜右僉都御史，巡撫延綏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Yan-Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of Yan-Sui.

sentences.zh: 河套常犯順，罷貢市十餘年。

translations.literal: The Ordos tribes often violated submission, and tribute trade had been suspended for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: The Ordos tribes had long defied submission, and border tribute trade had been suspended for over a decade.

sentences.zh: 後復松山，築邊城，諸部長恐，益侵軼。

translations.literal: Later Songshan was restored and border fortifications were built; the tribal chiefs were afraid and increased their raids.
translations.idiomatic: When Songshan was later restored and border fortifications were built, the tribal chiefs grew fearful and stepped up their raids.

sentences.zh: 至是，吉囊、卜莊等乞款。

translations.literal: At this time Jinang, Buzhuang, and others sued for peace.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Jinang, Buzhuang, and others petitioned for peace.

sentences.zh: 聞巡撫王見賓當去，請益切。

translations.literal: Hearing that Grand Coordinator Wang Jianbin was about to leave, their pleas grew more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Grand Coordinator Wang Jianbin was soon to depart, they pressed their appeals all the more urgently.

sentences.zh: 在寧夏者曰著宰，亦請之巡撫楊時寧。

translations.literal: The one at Ningxia called Chuzai also made the request to Grand Coordinator Yang Shining.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzai, based at Ningxia, likewise appealed to Grand Coordinator Yang Shining.

sentences.zh: 兩鎮交奏，給事中桂有根請聽邊臣自主。

translations.literal: Both garrison areas submitted memorials in turn; the supervising secretary Gui Yougen requested that frontier officials be allowed to decide for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Both garrisons submitted memorials in succession, and Supervising Secretary Gui Yougen asked that frontier officials be permitted to decide the matter on their own.

sentences.zh: 維城方代見賓，時寧亦遷去，以黃嘉善代，二人並申約束。

translations.literal: Weicheng was just replacing Jianbin; Shining had also been transferred, and Huang Jiashan was appointed in his place; the two men jointly reaffirmed the constraints.
translations.idiomatic: Weicheng had just succeeded Jianbin, and Shining had also been transferred; Huang Jiashan took his place, and the two men jointly reaffirmed the terms of the agreement.

sentences.zh: 維城又條善後六事，款事復堅。

translations.literal: Weicheng also set forth six items for follow-up measures, and the peace agreement was restored to firm footing.
translations.idiomatic: Weicheng also laid out six measures for securing the settlement, and the peace agreement was once again put on solid ground.

sentences.zh: 初，維城在宣府，與總兵官麻承恩不相能。

translations.literal: Initially, when Weicheng was at Xuanfu, he did not get along with Regional Commander Ma Chengen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while serving at Xuanfu, Weicheng had been on bad terms with Regional Commander Ma Chengen.

sentences.zh: 會承恩亦移鎮延綏。

translations.literal: It happened that Chengen was also transferred to command Yan-Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Chengen was then transferred to command Yan-Sui as well.

sentences.zh: 一日，維城見城外積沙及城，命余丁除之。

translations.literal: One day Weicheng saw sand piled outside the wall reaching up to the ramparts and ordered spare laborers to clear it away.
translations.idiomatic: One day Weicheng saw sand heaped outside the walls nearly level with the ramparts and ordered spare laborers to remove it.

sentences.zh: 承恩紿其眾曰：「食不宿飽，且塞沙可盡乎？

translations.literal: Chengen deceived his troops, saying: "You never get a full meal two nights running, and besides, can desert sand ever be cleared completely?
translations.idiomatic: Chengen deceived the men, telling them: "You never eat your fill two nights in a row — and can desert sand ever be cleared away entirely?

sentences.zh: 」卒遂噪。

translations.literal: " The soldiers then raised a clamor.
translations.idiomatic: " The soldiers thereupon raised a clamor.

sentences.zh: 維城曉之曰：「除城沙，以防寇耳，非謂塞上沙也。

translations.literal: Weicheng explained to them: "Clearing the sand at the wall is to guard against raiders — I do not mean to fill in all the desert sand.
translations.idiomatic: Weicheng reasoned with them: "Clearing the sand at the wall is to guard against raiders — I do not mean to fill in all the desert sand.

sentences.zh: 」卒悟而散。

translations.literal: " The soldiers understood and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: " The men understood and dispersed.

sentences.zh: 維城因自劾，帝慰留維城，治嘩者。

translations.literal: Weicheng thereupon impeached himself; the emperor comforted him and retained him in office, and punished the riotous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Weicheng then submitted a self-impeachment; the emperor reassured him and kept him in post, while punishing those who had raised the disturbance.

sentences.zh: 然維城竟坐是得疾，不數月卒。

translations.literal: Yet Weicheng ultimately fell ill on account of this affair and died within a few months.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Weicheng ultimately fell ill from the ordeal and died within a few months.

sentences.zh: 將吏入視其橐，僅俸數金，賻而歸其喪。

translations.literal: When officers entered and looked inside his traveling chest, there were only a few taels of salary; they contributed mourning gifts and sent his coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: When officers looked inside his traveling chest, they found only a few taels of salary; they contributed funeral gifts and sent his coffin home.

sentences.zh: 謝傑，字漢甫，長樂人。

translations.literal: Xie Jie, style Hanfu, a native of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jie, styled Hanfu, was a native of Changle.

sentences.zh: 萬曆初進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the early Wanli reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the early Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 除行人。

translations.literal: Appointed Bearer of Dispatches.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Bearer of Dispatches.

sentences.zh: 冊封琉球，卻其饋。

translations.literal: When invested with a mission to enfeoff Ryukyu, he declined their gifts.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to invest the king of Ryukyu, he refused their gifts.

sentences.zh: 其使入謝，仍以金饋，卒言於朝而返之。

translations.literal: When their envoys came to give thanks, they still offered gold; he reported this to the court and returned it.
translations.idiomatic: When Ryukyuan envoys came to give thanks, they again offered gold; he reported the matter to the court and sent it back.

sentences.zh: 歷兩京太常少卿。

translations.literal: He served successively as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in both capitals.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in both capitals.

sentences.zh: 南京歲祀懿文太子，以祠祭司官代，傑言：「祝版署御名，而遣賤者將事，於禮為褻。

translations.literal: For the annual sacrifices to the Crown Prince of Yi in Nanjing, sacrificial officials were sent in place of others; Jie said: "The prayer tablet bears the emperor's signature, yet you dispatch men of low rank to conduct the rite — by ritual standards this is disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: For the annual rites to the Crown Prince of Yi in Nanjing, sacrificial officials were substituted in the ceremony; Jie argued: "The prayer tablet bears the emperor's own name, yet men of low rank are sent to perform the rite — by the standards of ritual this is a profanation.

sentences.zh: 請如哀沖、莊敬二太子例，遣列侯。

translations.literal: I request that, following the precedents set for the Crown Princes Ai and Zhuangjing, a noble be dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that, following the precedents of the Crown Princes Ai and Zhuangjing, a noble be dispatched instead.

sentences.zh: 」帝是之，乃用南京五府僉書。

translations.literal: " The emperor agreed and accordingly used aides from the five offices of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved, and aides from Nanjing's five offices were accordingly assigned.

sentences.zh: 累遷順天府尹。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Magistrate of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Magistrate of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以右副都御史巡撫南、贛。

translations.literal: As Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he served as grand coordinator of Nan and Gan.
translations.idiomatic: As Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he served as grand coordinator of southern Jiangxi and Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 屬吏被薦者以賄謝，傑曰：「賄而後薦，干戈之盜；

translations.literal: A subordinate official who had been recommended tried to thank him with a bribe; Jie said: "Bribing before recommendation — that is robbery by force;
translations.idiomatic: When a subordinate he had recommended tried to thank him with a bribe, Jie said: "Bribing before recommendation is robbery at the point of a blade;

sentences.zh: 薦而後賄，衣冠之盜。

translations.literal: recommending before a bribe — that is robbery in scholar's robes.
translations.idiomatic: recommending before a bribe is robbery in scholar's robes.

sentences.zh: 」人以為名言。

translations.literal: " People regarded this as an immortal saying.
translations.idiomatic: " People took this for a saying worth remembering.

sentences.zh: 進南京刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Promoted to Right Vice Minister of the Ministry of Justice in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Minister of the Ministry of Justice in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 二十五年春，傑以帝荒於政事，疏陳十規。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-fifth year, Jie, considering the emperor negligent in state affairs, submitted a memorial setting forth ten admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-fifth year, finding the emperor neglectful of state affairs, Jie submitted a memorial laying out ten admonitions.

sentences.zh: 言：「前此兩宮色養維一，今則定省久曠，慶賀亦疏。

translations.literal: He said: "Before, your Majesty attended the two palaces in filial devotion without wavering; now the rites of morning and evening attendance have long been neglected, and congratulatory visits are also infrequent.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Before, your Majesty tended the two palaces with unwavering filial devotion; now the rites of morning and evening attendance have long gone unobserved, and congratulatory visits have grown rare.

sentences.zh: 孝安太后發引，並不親送。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Xiao'an's coffin was sent off, your Majesty did not personally escort it.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Xiao'an's coffin was sent on its final journey, your Majesty did not escort it in person.

sentences.zh: 前此太廟時饗皆躬親，今則皆遣代。

translations.literal: Before, seasonal offerings at the Imperial Ancestral Temple were all performed in person; now substitutes are always sent.
translations.idiomatic: Before, seasonal offerings at the Imperial Ancestral Temple were performed in person; now substitutes are always sent.

sentences.zh: 前此經筵臨御，聖學日勤，今則講官徒設，講席久虛。

translations.literal: Before, your Majesty presided at the Classics Colloquium and pursued sacred learning with daily diligence; now the lecturers exist in name only and the lecture seat has long stood empty.
translations.idiomatic: Before, your Majesty presided at the Classics Colloquium and pursued sacred learning with daily diligence; now the lecturers exist in name only and the lecture seat has long stood empty.

sentences.zh: 前此披星視朝，今則高拱深居，累年不出。

translations.literal: Before, you rose before dawn to hold court; now you dwell in deep seclusion, not emerging for years on end.
translations.idiomatic: Before, you rose before dawn to hold court; now you dwell in deep seclusion and have not emerged for years on end.

sentences.zh: 前此歲旱步禱郊壇，今則圜丘大報，久缺齋居；

translations.literal: Before, in years of drought you walked to the suburban altar to pray; now the Great Offering at the Circular Mound has long gone without the required fasting and seclusion;
translations.idiomatic: Before, in years of drought you walked to the suburban altar to pray; now the Great Offering at the Circular Mound has long gone without the required fasting and seclusion;

sentences.zh: 宸宮告災，亦忘修省。

translations.literal: when the palace reported disaster, you also forgot self-examination and reform.
translations.idiomatic: when the palace reported disaster, you also forgot self-examination and reform.

sentences.zh: 前此四方旱澇，多發帑金，今則采礦榷稅。

translations.literal: Before, when drought and flood struck the four quarters, you frequently disbursed treasury funds; now you impose mining levies and transit taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Before, when drought and flood struck the four quarters, you frequently disbursed treasury funds; now you impose mining levies and transit taxes.

sentences.zh: 前此用財有節，今則歲進月輸；

translations.literal: Before, public spending was restrained; now tribute arrives year by year and month by month;
translations.idiomatic: Before, public spending was restrained; now tribute arrives year by year and month by month;

sentences.zh: 而江右之磁，江南之纻，西蜀之扇，關中之絨，率取之逾額。

translations.literal: and the porcelain of Jiangyou, ramie cloth of Jiangnan, fans of western Shu, and woolens of Guanzhong — all are taken in excess of quota.
translations.idiomatic: and the porcelain of Jiangyou, ramie cloth of Jiangnan, fans of western Shu, and woolens of Guanzhong are all taken in excess of quota.

sentences.zh: 前此樂聞讜言，今則封事甫陳，嚴綸隨降，但經廢棄，永不賜環。

translations.literal: Before, you were glad to hear loyal remonstrance; now as soon as a sealed memorial is submitted, harsh decrees follow, and once dismissed, one is never recalled to office.
translations.idiomatic: Before, you were glad to hear loyal remonstrance; now as soon as a sealed memorial is submitted, harsh decrees follow, and once dismissed, one is never recalled to office.

sentences.zh: 前此撫恤宗室，恩義有加，今則楚藩見誣，中榼旋出，以市井奸宄，間骨肉懿親。

translations.literal: Before, you showed added grace and duty toward the imperial clan; now the Prince of Chu was falsely accused, eunuchs were promptly dispatched, and market-town scoundrels were used to come between blood kin.
translations.idiomatic: Before, you showed added grace and duty toward the imperial clan; now the Prince of Chu was falsely accused, eunuchs were promptly dispatched, and market-town scoundrels were used to come between blood kin.

sentences.zh: 前此官盛任使，下無曠鰥，今則大僚屢虛，庶官不補。

translations.literal: Before, posts were filled and men employed, with no vacant offices below; now senior posts sit empty and junior posts go unfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Before, posts were filled and men employed, with no vacant offices below; now senior posts sit empty and junior posts go unfilled.

sentences.zh: 是陛下孝親、尊祖，好學、勤政、敬天、愛民、節用、聽言、親親、賢賢，皆不克如初矣。

translations.literal: Thus your Majesty's filial piety toward parents, reverence for ancestors, love of learning, diligence in governance, reverence for Heaven, love of the people, frugality, willingness to heed counsel, cherishing of kin, and honoring of worthies — none can be maintained as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Thus your Majesty's filial piety toward parents, reverence for ancestors, love of learning, diligence in governance, reverence for Heaven, love of the people, frugality, willingness to heed counsel, cherishing of kin, and honoring of worthies — none can be maintained as at first.

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: " No response was given.

sentences.zh: 召為刑部左侍郎，擢戶部尚書督倉場。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Left Vice Minister of the Ministry of Justice, then promoted to Minister of Revenue to supervise the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as Left Vice Minister of the Ministry of Justice, then promoted to Minister of Revenue to supervise the granaries.

sentences.zh: 時四方遇災，率請改折，傑請歲運必三百萬以上方許議折，從之。

translations.literal: At that time regions everywhere encountering disaster generally requested conversion of grain tribute to silver; Jie requested that conversion be considered only when annual grain shipments exceeded three million shi; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: At that time regions stricken by disaster commonly petitioned to convert grain tribute to silver; Jie argued that conversion should be considered only when annual grain shipments exceeded three million shi, and this was approved.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，卒官。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 初，傑父教諭廷袞家居老矣，族人假其名逋賦。

translations.literal: Initially, Jie's father Tinggun, an instructor, was living at home in old age; clansmen used his name to evade tax payments.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jie's father Tinggun, a district instructor, was living at home in old age when clansmen used his name to evade tax payments.

sentences.zh: 縣令劉禹龍言於御史逮之。

translations.literal: The county magistrate Liu Yulong informed the censor, who had him arrested.
translations.idiomatic: County Magistrate Liu Yulong reported the matter to the censor, who had him arrested.

sentences.zh: 傑代訊，幾斃。

translations.literal: Jie went in his place for interrogation and nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: Jie went in his father's place for interrogation and nearly died.

sentences.zh: 後撫贛，禹龍家居，未嘗修隙，時服其量。

translations.literal: Later when Jie was grand coordinator of Gan, Yulong was living at home; Jie never nursed a grudge, and contemporaries admired his magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Jie served as grand coordinator of Ganzhou, Yulong was living at home; Jie never nursed a grudge, and contemporaries admired his magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 郭惟賢，字哲卿，晉江人。

translations.literal: Guo Weixian, style Zheqing, a native of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Weixian, styled Zheqing, was a native of Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the second year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 自清江知縣拜南京御史。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Qingjiang he was appointed Censor at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: From his post as magistrate of Qingjiang he was appointed censor at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 張居正既死，吳中行、趙用賢等猶未錄。

translations.literal: After Zhang Juzheng's death, Wu Zhonghang, Zhao Yongxian, and others had still not been restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Juzheng's death, Wu Zhonghang, Zhao Yongxian, and others had still not been restored to office.

sentences.zh: 會皇長子生，詔赦天下，惟賢因請召諸臣。

translations.literal: When the emperor's eldest son was born, an amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven; Weixian therefore requested that these officials be summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's eldest son was born and an amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven, Weixian petitioned that these officials be recalled.

sentences.zh: 馮保惡其言，謫江山丞。

translations.literal: Feng Bao hated his words and demoted him to assistant magistrate of Jiangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Bao resented his words and demoted him to assistant magistrate of Jiangshan.

sentences.zh: 保敗，還故官。

translations.literal: When Bao fell, he was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Bao fell from power, Weixian was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 劾左都御史陳炌希權臣指，論罷御史趙耀、趙應元，不可總憲紀。

translations.literal: He impeached Left Censor-in-Chief Chen Can for following the wishes of the power-holder and having censors Zhao Yao and Zhao Yingyuan dismissed; such conduct, he argued, was unfit for one who presides over the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Left Censor-in-Chief Chen Can for doing the power-holder's bidding in having Censors Zhao Yao and Zhao Yingyuan dismissed, arguing that such conduct was unfit for one who presided over the censorate.

sentences.zh: 炌罷去。

translations.literal: Can was dismissed and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Can was dismissed and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 又薦王錫爵、賈三近、孫鑨、何源、孫丕揚、耿定向、曾同亨、詹仰庇，皆獲召。

translations.literal: He also recommended Wang Xijue, Jia Sanjin, Sun Lin, He Yuan, Sun Piyang, Geng Dingxiang, Zeng Tongheng, and Zhan Yangbi; all were summoned to office.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended Wang Xijue, Jia Sanjin, Sun Lin, He Yuan, Sun Piyang, Geng Dingxiang, Zeng Tongheng, and Zhan Yangbi, all of whom were summoned to office.

sentences.zh: 主事董基諫內操被謫，惟賢救之，忤旨，調南京大理評事。

translations.literal: When the director Dong Ji remonstrated against inner-palace military drills and was banished, Weixian tried to save him; defying the imperial will, he was transferred to reviewing clerk in the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When Director Dong Ji remonstrated against inner-palace military drills and was banished, Weixian tried to save him; for defying the imperial will he was transferred to reviewing clerk in the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 給事中阮子孝、御史潘惟嶽等交章救。

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries Ruan Zixiao, the censor Pan Weiyue, and others submitted memorials in succession to intercede.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Ruan Zixiao, Censor Pan Weiyue, and others submitted memorials in succession to intercede.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，奪俸有差。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and withheld salaries by varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angered and withheld salaries in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 惟賢尋遷戶部主事，歷順天府丞。

translations.literal: Weixian was soon transferred to director in the Ministry of Revenue and served as vice magistrate of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Weixian was soon transferred to a directorship in the Ministry of Revenue and later served as vice magistrate of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二十年，以右僉都御史巡撫湖廣。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 景王封德安，土田倍諸藩，國絕賦額猶存。

translations.literal: When Prince Jing was enfeoffed at De'an, his land was double that of other princely establishments; though the state perished, the tax quotas still remained.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jing was enfeoffed at De'an, his landholdings were double those of other princely establishments; though the line had died out, the tax quotas still remained.

sentences.zh: 及帝弟潞王之國衛輝，悉以景賦予王。

translations.literal: When the emperor's younger brother, the Prince of Lu, went to his fief at Weihui, all of Jing's tax allotments were given to the prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's younger brother, the Prince of Lu, went to his fief at Weihui, all of the Jing establishment's tax allotments were assigned to him.

sentences.zh: 王奏賦不及額，帝為奪監司以下俸，責撫按急奏報。

translations.literal: The prince reported that collections fell short of quota; the emperor thereupon suspended the salaries of supervising officials and below, and ordered the grand coordinator and regional inspector to submit urgent reports.
translations.idiomatic: The prince reported that collections fell short of quota; the emperor thereupon suspended the salaries of supervising officials and below and ordered the grand coordinator and regional inspector to submit urgent reports.

sentences.zh: 惟賢言：「景府賦額皆奸民投獻，妄張其數。

translations.literal: Weixian said: "The tax quotas of the Jing establishment were all fraudulent gifts from scoundrels who inflated the figures.
translations.idiomatic: Weixian wrote: "The tax quotas of the Jing establishment were all fraudulent gifts from scoundrels who inflated the figures.

sentences.zh: 臣為王履畝，增賦二萬五千，非復如往者虛數，王反稱不足，何也？

translations.literal: I measured the fields for the prince myself and increased the levy by twenty-five thousand; this is no longer the hollow figure of old — yet the prince still claims it insufficient. Why?
translations.idiomatic: I measured the fields for the prince myself and increased the levy by twenty-five thousand — this is no longer the hollow figure of old — yet the prince still claims it insufficient. Why?

sentences.zh: 且潞去楚遠，莫若征之有司，轉輸潞府。

translations.literal: Moreover, Lu's fief is far from Chu; it would be better to collect through the local authorities and forward the revenue to the Prince of Lu's household.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Prince of Lu's fief is far from Huguang; it would be better to collect through local authorities and forward the revenue to his household.

sentences.zh: 《會典》皇莊及勛戚官莊，遇災蠲減視民田。

translations.literal: The Collected Statutes provide that imperial estates and official estates of meritorious kin, when disaster strikes, receive remissions equal to those for commoners' fields.
translations.idiomatic: The Collected Statutes provide that imperial estates and official estates of meritorious kin, when disaster strikes, receive remissions equal to those granted commoners' fields.

sentences.zh: 今襄、漢水溢，王佃民流亡過半，請蠲如例。

translations.literal: Now the Xiang and Han rivers have overflowed; more than half of the prince's tenant farmers have fled — I request remission according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Xiang and Han rivers have overflowed; more than half of the prince's tenant farmers have fled — I request remission according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「長沙、寶慶、衡州三衛軍戍武岡，而永州、寧遠諸衛遠戍廣西，瘴癘死無數。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Soldiers of the three guards of Changsha, Baoqing, and Hengzhou garrison Wugang, while those of Yongzhou, Ningyuan, and other guards garrison far-off Guangxi — countless have died of malarial pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote: "Soldiers of the three guards of Changsha, Baoqing, and Hengzhou garrison Wugang, while those of Yongzhou, Ningyuan, and other guards garrison far-off Guangxi — countless have died of malarial pestilence.

sentences.zh: 請分番叠戍武岡，罷其戍廣西者。

translations.literal: I request rotating shifts to garrison Wugang in relays, and abolishing the Guangxi garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: I request rotating shifts to garrison Wugang in relays and abolishing the Guangxi garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 」帝悉報許。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved all in reply.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved all of these in reply.

sentences.zh: 承天守備中官以征興邸舊賦，請罪潛江知縣及諸佃民，旨下撫按勾捕。

translations.literal: The eunuch commandant defending Chengtian, collecting old levies from the former residence of the Xing establishment, requested punishment of the magistrate of Qianjiang and various tenant farmers; an imperial order was sent down for the grand coordinator and inspector to arrest them.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch commandant defending Chengtian, collecting old levies from the former Xing establishment, requested punishment of the magistrate of Qianjiang and various tenant farmers; an imperial order was sent down for the grand coordinator and regional inspector to arrest them.

sentences.zh: 惟賢言：「臣撫楚，事無不當問。

translations.literal: Weixian said: "I govern Huguang; there is no matter I should not inquire into.
translations.idiomatic: Weixian wrote: "As grand coordinator of Huguang, there is no matter I should not inquire into.

sentences.zh: 今中官問，而臣等為勾捕，臣實不能。

translations.literal: Now the eunuch inquires while we are made to arrest people — I truly cannot do this.
translations.idiomatic: Now the eunuch conducts the inquiry while we are made to arrest people — I truly cannot do this.

sentences.zh: 」帝直其言而止。

translations.literal: " The emperor upheld his words and halted the matter.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor upheld his words and halted the matter.

sentences.zh: 尋請以太和山香稅充王府逋祿，免加派小民，又請以周敦頤父輔成從祀啟聖。

translations.literal: Soon he requested that incense taxes from Mount Taihe cover the prince's household's arrears in stipends, sparing additional levies on commoners; he also requested that Zhou Dunyi's father Fucheng be granted accompanying sacrifice in the Confucian shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he requested that incense taxes from Mount Taihe cover the prince's household arrears in stipends, sparing additional levies on commoners; he also asked that Zhou Dunyi's father Fucheng be granted accompanying sacrifice in the Confucian shrine.

sentences.zh: 詔皆從焉。

translations.literal: Edicts approved all of these.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial edicts approved all of these requests.

sentences.zh: 入為左僉都御史。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 言行取不宜久停，言官不宜久系，臺員不宜久缺。

translations.literal: He said that provincial appointments should not be suspended too long, remonstrating officials should not be detained too long, and censorate posts should not remain vacant too long.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that provincial appointments should not be suspended too long, remonstrating officials should not be detained too long, and censorate posts should not remain vacant too long.

sentences.zh: 已，復言天下多故，乃自大僚至監司率有缺不補，政日廢弛，且建言獲譴者不下百餘人，效忠者皆永棄。

translations.literal: Subsequently he again said that with turmoil everywhere, from senior officials down to supervising commissioners posts commonly went unfilled and governance daily grew lax; moreover, those punished for offering counsel numbered no fewer than a hundred, and the loyal were cast aside forever.
translations.idiomatic: He then added that with turmoil everywhere, from senior officials down to supervising commissioners posts commonly went unfilled and governance daily grew lax; moreover, those punished for offering counsel numbered no fewer than a hundred, and the loyal were cast aside forever.

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept this.

sentences.zh: 尋遷左副都御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 請早建皇儲，慎簡輔弼，亟行考選，盡下推舉諸疏。

translations.literal: He requested an early establishment of the crown prince, careful selection of assistants, prompt conduct of examinations and selections, and forwarding of all recommendation memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He requested an early establishment of the crown prince, careful selection of assistants, prompt conduct of examinations and selections, and forwarding of all recommendation memorials.
