sentences.zh: 俱不報。

translations.literal: None received a response.
translations.idiomatic: None of these received a response.

sentences.zh: 久之，以憂歸。

translations.literal: After a long time, he returned home on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he resigned and went home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 起戶部左侍郎，未上卒。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as Left Vice Minister of Revenue, but died before assuming office.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Left Vice Minister of Revenue but died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 贈右都御史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，謚恭定。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, he was given the posthumous name Gongding.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tianqi reign he was granted the posthumous title Gongding.

sentences.zh: 萬象春，字仁甫，無錫人。

translations.literal: Wan Xiangchun, courtesy name Renfu, was a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Xiangchun, whose courtesy name was Renfu, came from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 萬曆五年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，授工科給事中。

translations.literal: He was selected as a Hanlin probationer and appointed Supervising Secretary in the Department of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a Hanlin probationer, he was appointed Supervising Secretary in the Department of Works.

sentences.zh: 皇女生，詔戶部、光祿寺各進銀十萬兩。

translations.literal: When an imperial daughter was born, an edict ordered the Ministry of Revenue and the Court of Imperial Entertainments each to present one hundred thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial daughter was born, the throne ordered the Ministry of Revenue and the Court of Imperial Entertainments each to present one hundred thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 象春力諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Xiangchun remonstrated forcefully, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangchun remonstrated forcefully, but his advice went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 屢遷禮科都給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Secretary-in-Chief of the Department of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to become Supervising Secretary-in-Chief of the Department of Rites.

sentences.zh: 鄭貴妃有盛寵，而帝耽於酒。

translations.literal: Consort Zheng enjoyed great favor, while the emperor indulged himself in wine.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zheng enjoyed extraordinary favor, while the emperor sank deeper into drink.

sentences.zh: 象春因慈寧宮災疏諫，報聞。

translations.literal: Xiangchun submitted a memorial of remonstrance on account of the fire at Cining Palace; the court acknowledged receipt.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangchun memorialized in remonstrance after the fire at Cining Palace; the court acknowledged receipt but took no action.

sentences.zh: 時宗室繁衍，歲祿不繼，象春議變通。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial clansmen had multiplied, and annual stipends could no longer keep pace; Xiangchun proposed flexible measures.
translations.idiomatic: As the imperial clansmen multiplied and annual stipends could no longer keep pace, Xiangchun proposed flexible reforms.

sentences.zh: 會河南巡撫褚鈇亦奏其事，帝即命象春遍詣河南、山西、陜西諸王府，計畫以聞。

translations.literal: It happened that Chu Tie, grand coordinator of Henan, also memorialized on the matter, and the emperor immediately ordered Xiangchun to visit all the princely establishments in Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi, devise plans, and report.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu Tie, grand coordinator of Henan, also memorialized on the matter, the emperor immediately ordered Xiangchun to visit every princely establishment in Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi, work out a plan, and report back.

sentences.zh: 象春抵河南，方集議，而周府諸宗人疑鈇疏出宗正睦挈意，群毆睦挈幾死。

translations.literal: When Xiangchun reached Henan and was just convening deliberations, the clansmen of the Zhou establishment suspected that Chu's memorial had come from the intent of Mu Jie, Director of the Imperial Clan Court, and mobbed and beat Mu Jie nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangchun reached Henan and was convening deliberations, the Zhou princely clansmen suspected that Chu's memorial reflected the wishes of Mu Jie, Director of the Imperial Clan Court, and mobbed and beat him nearly to death.

sentences.zh: 象春以狀聞，帝為奪諸人歲祿。

translations.literal: Xiangchun reported the situation, and the emperor suspended the annual stipends of all those involved.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangchun reported what had happened, and the emperor suspended the annual stipends of all those involved.

sentences.zh: 象春復以次詣秦、晉諸藩，奏上便宜十五事，多著為令。

translations.literal: Xiangchun then proceeded in turn to the Qin and Jin princely establishments, submitted fifteen expedient measures, and many were established as regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangchun then visited the Qin and Jin establishments in turn, submitted fifteen practical proposals, and many were written into law.

sentences.zh: 真人張國祥乞三年一覲，象春言左道無民社寄，不當在述職之列。

translations.literal: The Daoist patriarch Zhang Guoxiang requested an audience every three years; Xiangchun said that heterodox ways had no charge over the people or the state and should not be included in the roster for tribute audiences.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist patriarch Zhang Guoxiang asked to present tribute once every three years; Xiangchun argued that heterodox teachings had no charge over the people or the state and should not be included among those reporting for duty.

sentences.zh: 時詔許後父永年伯王偉乘肩輿，象春言：「勛戚不乘輿，祖制也。

translations.literal: At the time an edict permitted the empress's father, Wang Wei, Earl of Yongnian, to ride in a sedan chair; Xiangchun said: "Meritorious kin do not ride the imperial conveyance — this is ancestral institution.
translations.idiomatic: At the time an edict permitted the empress's father, Wang Wei, Earl of Yongnian, to ride in a sedan chair; Xiangchun wrote: "Meritorious kin do not ride the imperial conveyance — that is ancestral institution.

sentences.zh: 固安伯陳景行、武清伯李偉，太后父，衰白封，始賜肩輿。

translations.literal: Chen Jingxing, Earl of Gu'an, and Li Wei, Earl of Wuqing — fathers of the empress dowager — were already gray-haired when enfeoffed and only then were granted sedan chairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxing, Earl of Gu'an, and Li Wei, Earl of Wuqing — both fathers of the empress dowager — were already white-haired when enfeoffed and only then were granted sedan chairs.

sentences.zh: 定國公徐文璧班首重臣，嗣爵久，故亦蒙殊典。

translations.literal: Xu Wenbi, Duke of Dingguo, was the leading statesman of his generation; having held his title for a long time, he too received an exceptional honor.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wenbi, Duke of Dingguo, stood at the head of the senior statesmen; having held his title for many years, he too had received an exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 今偉非三人比，乞寢前命。

translations.literal: Wang Wei cannot be compared with those three men; I beg that the prior order be revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei cannot be compared with those three men; I beg that the prior order be withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 」皆不許。

translations.literal: " None of these requests was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " None of these requests was granted.

sentences.zh: 孟秋將享廟，帝齋宿宮中，象春言當在便殿，不當於內寢。

translations.literal: As mid-autumn approached and the temple sacrifice was due, the emperor fasted and lodged within the palace; Xiangchun said he should stay in a side hall and not in the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: As mid-autumn approached and the temple sacrifice drew near, the emperor fasted and lodged within the palace; Xiangchun argued that he should stay in a side hall rather than in the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，停俸三月。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angry and suspended his salary for three months.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and suspended his salary for three months.

sentences.zh: 已，因災異，言：「外吏貪殘不當遣緹騎逮問，宮禁邃密不當宿重兵，廷臣建言貶黜當敘遷，內臣有犯當付外廷按治。

translations.literal: Later, citing calamities and portents, he said: "Corrupt and cruel provincial officials should not be seized and interrogated by imperial runners; the deep palace precincts should not quarter heavy troops; court officials punished for offering counsel should be restored to rank; and offending eunuchs should be handed over to the outer court for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Later, citing calamities and portents, he wrote: "Corrupt and cruel provincial officials should not be seized and interrogated by imperial runners; the deep palace precincts should not quarter heavy troops; court officials punished for offering counsel should be restored to rank; and offending eunuchs should be handed over to the outer court for trial.

sentences.zh: 」帝報聞。

translations.literal: " The emperor acknowledged receipt.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor acknowledged receipt but took no action.

sentences.zh: 象春在諫垣久，前後七十餘疏，多關軍國計。

translations.literal: Xiangchun served long in the remonstrance offices and submitted more than seventy memorials in all, most of them bearing on military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangchun served long in the remonstrance offices and submitted more than seventy memorials in all, most of them bearing on military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 請復建文年號，加景帝廟謚，尤為時所稱。

translations.literal: His requests to restore the Jianwen reign title and add a temple posthumous title for Emperor Jing were especially praised by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: His requests to restore the Jianwen reign title and add a temple posthumous title for Emperor Jing won him especial praise.

sentences.zh: 出為山東參政。

translations.literal: He was sent out to serve as Administration Commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as Administration Commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 妖賊郭大通為亂，計擒之。

translations.literal: The demonic bandit Guo Datong raised rebellion, and Xiangchun captured him by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerer-rebel Guo Datong raised an uprising, and Xiangchun captured him by stratagem.

sentences.zh: 歷山西左布政使。

translations.literal: He served as Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，以右副都御史巡撫山東。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 倭躪朝鮮，濱海郡邑悉戒嚴。

translations.literal: The Japanese ravaged Korea, and coastal prefectures and counties all went on alert.
translations.idiomatic: When Japanese forces ravaged Korea, every coastal prefecture and county went on alert.

sentences.zh: 象春拊軍民，供饋運，應機立辦。

translations.literal: Xiangchun reassured troops and civilians, supplied transport and provisions, and handled matters on the spot as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangchun reassured troops and civilians, supplied transport and provisions, and handled each emergency as it arose.

sentences.zh: 中使陳增以礦稅至，象春疏論其害。

translations.literal: The eunuch envoy Chen Zeng arrived to collect mining taxes, and Xiangchun submitted a memorial on the harm they caused.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch envoy Chen Zeng arrived to collect mining taxes, Xiangchun memorialized on the harm they caused.

sentences.zh: 福山知縣韋國賢忤增被侵辱，象春力保持之，增遂劾國賢沮撓，象春黨庇。

translations.literal: Wei Guoxian, magistrate of Fushan, offended Chen Zeng and was humiliated; Xiangchun forcefully protected him, whereupon Chen impeached Wei for obstruction and Xiangchun for factional shielding.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guoxian, magistrate of Fushan, offended Chen Zeng and was humiliated; Xiangchun forcefully protected him, whereupon Chen impeached Wei for obstruction and Xiangchun for shielding him out of factional loyalty.

sentences.zh: 詔逮國賢，奪象春俸，遂引疾歸。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wei's arrest and suspended Xiangchun's salary; he then pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Wei's arrest and suspended Xiangchun's salary; he then pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 起南京工部右侍郎，未上卒。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as Right Vice Minister of Works at Nanjing, but died before assuming office.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Right Vice Minister of Works at Nanjing but died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 贈右都御史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 鐘化民，字維新，仁和人。

translations.literal: Zhong Huamin, courtesy name Weixin, was a native of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Huamin, whose courtesy name was Weixin, came from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 萬曆八年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the eighth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授惠安知縣，多異政。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Hui'an and carried out many outstanding policies.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed magistrate of Hui'an, he carried out many outstanding policies.

sentences.zh: 御史安九域薦於朝，以俸未及期，移知樂平，治復最。

translations.literal: Censor An Jiuyu recommended him to the court, but because his term of salary had not yet expired he was transferred to serve as magistrate of Leping, where his governance again ranked highest.
translations.idiomatic: Censor An Jiuyu recommended him to the court, but because his term had not yet expired he was transferred to Leping, where his governance again ranked highest.

sentences.zh: 征授御史。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed an imperial censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital and appointed an imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 與同官何卓、王慎德交章請建儲，不報。

translations.literal: Together with his colleagues He Zhuo and Wang Shende he submitted successive memorials requesting the establishment of the crown prince, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: Together with his colleagues He Zhuo and Wang Shende he submitted successive memorials requesting the establishment of the crown prince, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 出視陜西茶馬，言：「邊塞土寒，獨畜馬為業。

translations.literal: Sent out to inspect the tea-horse trade in Shaanxi, he said: "The borderlands are cold, and the people rely solely on horse breeding for their livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out to inspect the tea-horse trade in Shaanxi, he wrote: "The borderlands are cold, and the people rely solely on horse breeding for their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 今慮其闌出為厲禁，於是民間孳息與境內貿易俱廢，公私緩急亦無所資。

translations.literal: Now, fearing that horses would slip across the border, strict prohibitions have been imposed; as a result private breeding and trade within the region have both been abolished, and neither public nor private needs can be met in an emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Now, fearing that horses would slip across the border, strict prohibitions have been imposed; as a result private breeding and trade within the region have both been abolished, and neither public nor private needs can be met in an emergency.

sentences.zh: 請聽逾境販鬻，特不得入番中。

translations.literal: I request that cross-border sale be permitted, provided only that horses may not enter tribal territory.
translations.idiomatic: I request that cross-border sale be permitted, provided only that horses may not enter tribal territory.

sentences.zh: 又曩寧夏乏餉，歲發萬金易米二萬七千石，後所司幹沒，濫征之民。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the past Ningxia lacked rations, and ten thousand taels of gold were sent each year to exchange for twenty-seven thousand shi of grain; later the responsible officials embezzled the funds and indiscriminately levied the people.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the past Ningxia lacked rations, and ten thousand taels of gold were sent each year to exchange for twenty-seven thousand shi of grain; later the responsible officials embezzled the funds and indiscriminately levied the people.

sentences.zh: 請以墾田粟補之，永停征派。

translations.literal: I request that grain from reclaimed fields be used to make up the shortfall and that the levies be permanently stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that reclaimed-field grain be used to cover the shortfall and that the levies be abolished permanently.

sentences.zh: 」俱報可。

translations.literal: " Both proposals were approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The court approved both requests.

sentences.zh: 巡按山東，歲旱，請蠲振先發後聞。

translations.literal: While inspecting Shandong, in a year of drought he requested that tax remissions and relief be dispensed first and reported afterward.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting Shandong during a drought year, he requested that tax remissions and relief be dispensed first and reported afterward.

sentences.zh: 坐寧夏時取官銀交際，為尚寶丞周弘禴所劾，調行人司正。

translations.literal: He was implicated for taking official silver for social purposes while in Ningxia, was impeached by Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia Zhou Hongdiao, and was transferred to serve as Recorder of the Messenger Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was implicated for taking official silver for social purposes while in Ningxia, was impeached by Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia Zhou Hongdiao, and was transferred to serve as Recorder of the Messenger Office.

sentences.zh: 累遷儀制郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted through several ranks to Director of Ceremonies in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several ranks to become Director of Ceremonies in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 沈王呈堯由支庶嗣，請封其庶子為郡王，化民持不可。

translations.literal: Cheng Yao, Prince of Shen, had succeeded from a collateral line and requested that his secondary son be enfeoffed as a commandery prince; Huamin objected that this should not be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yao, Prince of Shen, had succeeded from a collateral line and asked that his secondary son be enfeoffed as a commandery prince; Huamin objected that this should not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 帝傳諭曰：「第予虛名，令藉是婚娶耳。

translations.literal: The emperor sent word through a messenger, saying: "I would only give him an empty title so he can marry by it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent word through a messenger, saying: "I would only give him an empty title so he can marry by it.

sentences.zh: 」化民奏曰：「沈王子與元子孰親？

translations.literal: " Huamin memorialized, saying: "Which is closer — the Prince of Shen's son or the heir apparent?
translations.idiomatic: " Huamin memorialized, saying: "Which is closer — the Prince of Shen's son or the heir apparent?

sentences.zh: 王子不即封，慮妨婚娶，元子不即立，不慮妨豫教乎？

translations.literal: If the prince's son is not promptly enfeoffed for fear of blocking marriage, is the heir apparent not promptly established without fear of blocking his early education?
translations.idiomatic: If the prince's son is not promptly enfeoffed for fear of blocking marriage, is the heir apparent not promptly established without fear of blocking his early education?

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，以化民辭直，無以難。

translations.literal: " The emperor grew angry, but since Huamin's words were blunt and straight, he had no way to rebut them.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor grew angry, but since Huamin's words were blunt and straight, he had no way to rebut them.

sentences.zh: 帝命並封三王，化民與顧允成等面詰王錫爵於朝房。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the simultaneous enfeoffment of three princes, and Huamin, together with Gu Yuncheng and others, confronted Wang Xijue face to face in the court corridor.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ordered the simultaneous enfeoffment of three princes, Huamin, together with Gu Yuncheng and others, confronted Wang Xijue face to face in the court corridor.

sentences.zh: 尋進光祿丞。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，河南大饑，人相食，命化民兼河南道御史往振。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year a great famine struck Henan, and people ate one another; the emperor ordered Huamin to serve concurrently as Henan circuit censor and go to provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year a great famine struck Henan, and people ate one another; the emperor ordered Huamin to serve concurrently as Henan circuit censor and go to provide relief.

sentences.zh: 荒政具舉，民大悅。

translations.literal: Famine administration was fully carried out, and the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He carried out famine relief in full, and the people were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 既竣，繪圖以進。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, he submitted illustrated reports.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, he submitted illustrated reports to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，褒諭者再。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him and commended him twice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him and commended him twice.

sentences.zh: 擢太常少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，以右僉都御史巡撫河南，討平南陽礦盜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Henan, and he suppressed the mining bandits of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of Henan, where he suppressed the mining bandits of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 夾河賊嘯聚數千人，復督兵破之。

translations.literal: Bandits at Jiahe gathered in the thousands with shouts and clamor; he again led troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits at Jiahe gathered in the thousands, he again led troops and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 時方采礦，抗疏力諫。

translations.literal: Mining was then underway, and he submitted a forceful memorial in opposition.
translations.idiomatic: Mining was then underway, and he submitted a forceful memorial in opposition.

sentences.zh: 化民短小精悍，多智計。

translations.literal: Huamin was short, compact, and sharp, and full of clever stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Huamin was short, compact, and sharp, and full of clever stratagems.

sentences.zh: 居官勤厲，所至有聲。

translations.literal: Diligent and exacting in office, he won a reputation wherever he served.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent and exacting in office, he won a reputation wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 遍歷八府，延父老問疾苦。

translations.literal: He visited all eight prefectures and summoned elders to inquire into their hardships.
translations.idiomatic: He visited all eight prefectures and summoned elders to inquire into their hardships.

sentences.zh: 勞瘁卒官，士民相率頌於朝。

translations.literal: He worked himself to exhaustion and died in office; officials and commoners successively praised him at court.
translations.idiomatic: He worked himself to exhaustion and died in office; officials and commoners successively praised him at court.

sentences.zh: 詔贈右副都御史，賜祠曰忠惠。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him the title of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and bestowed on his shrine the name Zhonghui.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously granted him the title of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and bestowed on his shrine the name Zhonghui, Loyal and Kind.

sentences.zh: 吳達可，字安節，宜興人，尚書儼從孫也。

translations.literal: Wu Dake, courtesy name Anjie, was a native of Yixing and a grand-nephew of Minister Wu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Dake, whose courtesy name was Anjie, came from Yixing and was a grand-nephew of Minister Wu Yan.

sentences.zh: 萬曆五年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 歷知會稽、上高、豐城，並有聲。

translations.literal: He served successively as magistrate of Kuaiji, Shanggao, and Fengcheng, winning a reputation in each post.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as magistrate of Kuaiji, Shanggao, and Fengcheng, winning a reputation in each post.

sentences.zh: 選授御史。

translations.literal: He was selected and appointed an imperial censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected and appointed an imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 疏請御經筵勤學，時與大臣臺諫面議政務，報聞。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial requesting that the emperor attend the Classics Lectures and study diligently, and meet regularly with ministers and censorial officials to discuss state affairs face to face; the court acknowledged receipt.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized requesting that the emperor attend the Classics Lectures, study diligently, and meet regularly with ministers and censorial officials to discuss state affairs face to face; the court acknowledged receipt but took no action.

sentences.zh: 大學士趙誌臯久疾乞休，未得請。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhao Zhigao had long been ill and requested retirement, but his request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhao Zhigao had long been ill and requested retirement, but his request was not granted.

sentences.zh: 達可力言志臯衰庸，宜罷，不納。

translations.literal: Dake forcefully argued that Zhao was decrepit and mediocre and should be dismissed, but this was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Dake forcefully argued that Zhao was decrepit and mediocre and should be dismissed, but the emperor would not accept it.

sentences.zh: 二十八年正月，請因始和布令，舉皇長子冊立冠婚禮，簡輔臣補臺諫，撤礦稅中使，不報。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-eighth year he requested that, at the Beginning of Harmony, edicts be issued to carry out the investiture, capping, and marriage of the eldest imperial son, select assistant ministers, fill censorial posts, and withdraw the eunuch envoys collecting mining taxes; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-eighth year he requested that, at the Beginning of Harmony, edicts be issued to carry out the investiture, capping, and marriage of the eldest imperial son, select assistant ministers, fill censorial posts, and withdraw the eunuch envoys collecting mining taxes; there was no response.

sentences.zh: 視鹽長蘆。

translations.literal: He inspected salt administration at Changlu.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected salt administration at Changlu.

sentences.zh: 歲侵，繪上饑民十四圖，力請振貸。

translations.literal: In a year of crop failure he submitted fourteen paintings of starving people and forcefully requested relief and loans.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of crop failure he submitted fourteen paintings of starving people and forcefully requested relief and loans.

sentences.zh: 稅使馬堂、張日華議加鹽稅，奸商妄稱嘉靖中大同用兵貸其貲三萬六千金，請於鹽課補給，戶部許之。

translations.literal: The tax agents Ma Tang and Zhang Rihua proposed raising the salt tax; scheming merchants falsely claimed that during the Jiajing reign the campaign at Datong had borrowed thirty-six thousand jin of their capital, and requested repayment from salt revenues; the Ministry of Revenue approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The tax agents Ma Tang and Zhang Rihua proposed raising the salt tax; scheming merchants falsely claimed that during the Jiajing reign the campaign at Datong had borrowed thirty-six thousand jin of their capital and asked that it be repaid from salt revenues; the Ministry of Revenue approved the request.

sentences.zh: 達可皆抗爭，事得已。

translations.literal: Dake resisted all of these proposals, and the matters were dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Dake resisted all of these proposals, and the matters were dropped.

sentences.zh: 改按江西。

translations.literal: He was transferred to conduct an inspection in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to conduct an inspection in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 稅使潘相毆折輔國將軍謀圮肢，並系宗人宗達，誣以劫課，劾上饒知縣李鴻主使。

translations.literal: The tax agent Pan Xiang beat and broke the limbs of Mou Pi, Auxiliary State General, and also detained the clansman Zongda, falsely accusing him of robbing tax collection and impeaching Li Hong, magistrate of Shangrao, as the mastermind.
translations.idiomatic: The tax agent Pan Xiang beat and broke the limbs of Mou Pi, Auxiliary State General, and also detained the clansman Zongda, falsely accusing him of robbing tax collection and impeaching Li Hong, magistrate of Shangrao, as the mastermind.

sentences.zh: 帝切責謀圮等，奪鴻官。

translations.literal: The emperor severely rebuked Mou Pi and the others and stripped Li Hong of his office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor severely rebuked Mou Pi and the others and stripped Li Hong of his office.

sentences.zh: 達可言：「宗人無故受刑，又重之以詰責，將使天潢人人自危。

translations.literal: Dake said: "A clansman was punished without cause, and on top of that was subjected to stern rebuke; this will make every member of the imperial lineage feel endangered.
translations.idiomatic: Dake wrote: "A clansman was punished without cause, and on top of that was subjected to stern rebuke; this will make every member of the imperial lineage feel endangered.

sentences.zh: 鴻無辜，不當黜。

translations.literal: Li Hong is innocent and should not be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hong is innocent and should not be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 願亟正相罪，復鴻官。

translations.literal: I beg that Pan Xiang's guilt be promptly established and Li Hong's office restored.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Pan Xiang be promptly punished and Li Hong's office restored.

sentences.zh: 」同官湯兆京亦極論相罪，且言遼東高淮、陜西梁永、山東陳增、廣東李鳳、雲南楊榮皆元惡，為民害，不可一日留。

translations.literal: " His colleague Tang Zhaojing also argued forcefully for Pan Xiang's guilt, and further said that Gao Huai in Liaodong, Liang Yong in Shaanxi, Chen Zeng in Shandong, Li Feng in Guangdong, and Yang Rong in Yunnan were all arch-villains and scourges to the people who could not be allowed to remain even a day.
translations.idiomatic: " His colleague Tang Zhaojing also argued forcefully for Pan Xiang's guilt, and further said that Gao Huai in Liaodong, Liang Yong in Shaanxi, Chen Zeng in Shandong, Li Feng in Guangdong, and Yang Rong in Yunnan were all arch-villains and scourges to the people who could not be allowed to remain even a day.

sentences.zh: 皆弗聽。

translations.literal: None of this was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: None of this was heeded.

sentences.zh: 鴻，吳人，大學士申時行之婿。

translations.literal: Li Hong was a native of Wu and the son-in-law of Grand Secretary Shen Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hong was a native of Wu and the son-in-law of Grand Secretary Shen Shixing.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十六年舉北闈鄉試，為吏部郎中高桂所攻。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Wanli he passed the northern provincial examination, and was attacked by Gao Gui, a director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Wanli he passed the northern provincial examination, and was attacked by Gao Gui, a director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 後七年成進士。

translations.literal: Seven years later he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years later he received his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 至是，抗相，以強直稱。

translations.literal: On this occasion he resisted Pan Xiang and was praised for his firm integrity.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion he resisted Pan Xiang and was praised for his firm integrity.

sentences.zh: 相又請開廣信銅塘山，采取大木，鑿泰和斌姥山石膏，達可復極諫不可，閣臣亦爭之，乃寢。

translations.literal: Pan Xiang also requested opening Tongtang Mountain in Guangxin to harvest timber and quarrying gypsum at Binlao Mountain in Taihe; Dake again memorialized forcefully that this must not be allowed, the grand secretaries also objected, and the proposal was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Xiang also requested opening Tongtang Mountain in Guangxin to harvest timber and quarrying gypsum at Binlao Mountain in Taihe; Dake again memorialized forcefully against it, the grand secretaries also objected, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 還掌河南道事。

translations.literal: He returned to take charge of affairs in the Henan section.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to take charge of the Henan section.

sentences.zh: 佐溫純大計京官。

translations.literal: He assisted Wen Chun in the grand evaluation of capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: He assisted Wen Chun in conducting the grand evaluation of capital officials.

sentences.zh: 尋陳新政要機，痛規首輔沈一貫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he set forth the essential points of the new administration and sharply admonished Chief Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon set forth the essential points of the new administration and sharply admonished Chief Grand Secretary Shen Yiguan.

sentences.zh: 疏留中。

translations.literal: The memorial was kept at court.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was shelved at court.

sentences.zh: 擢太僕少卿，再遷南京太僕卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and later transferred to the same post in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and later transferred to the Nanjing post.

sentences.zh: 召改光祿，進通政使。

translations.literal: He was summoned and transferred to the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then advanced to Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the Court of Imperial Entertainments and then promoted to Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 鎮撫史晉以罪罷，妄投封章詆朝貴。

translations.literal: The guard commander Shi Jin had been dismissed for an offense and recklessly submitted a sealed memorial slandering court dignitaries.
translations.idiomatic: Guard commander Shi Jin, dismissed for misconduct, recklessly submitted a sealed memorial slandering senior officials at court.

sentences.zh: 達可封其疏而劾之，晉尋得罪。

translations.literal: Dake sealed his memorial and impeached him; Jin was soon punished.
translations.idiomatic: Dake sealed the memorial and impeached him; Jin was soon punished.

sentences.zh: 奏請正疏式、屏讒邪、重駁正、懲奸宄數事，帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting correction of memorial format, removal of slanderers, renewed weight for rebuttal and review, and punishment of evil-doers; the emperor praised and accepted these proposals.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on correcting memorial format, removing slanderers, restoring the weight of rebuttal and review, and punishing wrongdoers; the emperor praised and accepted his proposals.

sentences.zh: 尋上疏乞休去。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he submitted a memorial requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He soon submitted a memorial asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈右副都御史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted the rank of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously granted the rank of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：龐尚鵬諸人歷官中外，才諝幹局，咸有可稱。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Pang Shangpeng and the others served both in the capital and in the provinces; talented and capable in practical affairs, each had achievements worth noting.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Pang Shangpeng and the others served both at court and in the provinces; capable and practical in affairs, each had achievements worth noting.

sentences.zh: 賈三近陳時政，多長者之言，其言資格，深中積弊。

translations.literal: When Jia Sanjin addressed current policy, much of what he said was the counsel of a seasoned elder; his remarks on rank and qualification struck deeply at long-standing abuses.
translations.idiomatic: In addressing current policy, Jia Sanjin spoke often with the wisdom of a seasoned elder; his remarks on rank and qualification cut to the heart of long-standing abuses.

sentences.zh: 謝傑卻屬吏饋，亦無愧楊震云。

translations.literal: Xie Jie refused gifts from subordinate officials, and in this too he was no unworthy successor to Yang Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jie's refusal of gifts from subordinate officials likewise did honor to the example of Yang Zhen.
